q026.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains 30 CSV files in OneLake. The files are updated daily.

You create a Microsoft Power BI semantic model named Model1 that uses the CSV files as a data source. You configure incremental refresh for Model1 and publish the model to a Premium capacity in the Fabric tenant.

When you initiate a refresh of Model1, the refresh fails after running out of resources.

What is a possible cause of the failure?
options: Only refresh complete days is selected.
XMLA Endpoint is set to Read Only.
The delta type of the column used to partition the data has changed.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Query folding is NOT occurring.

Why it is correct: Incremental refresh works by filtering the source with the RangeStart and RangeEnd parameters so that each partition only requests its own slice of data. This only saves resources when the filter is pushed down to the source (query folding). If folding does not occur, Power BI has to load all the data from the source into the mashup engine and apply the filter there, for every partition, which is very slow and consumes a large amount of memory and CPU. The result is a refresh that takes too long or fails by running out of resources, exactly as the troubleshooting guidance for incremental refresh describes. Note that flat files such as the 30 CSV files do not support query folding, which is the typical cause in this scenario.

  • Official documentation: Troubleshoot incremental refresh and real-time data - loading data takes too long and Query folding in Power Query
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Query folding is occurring.

Why it is incorrect: Query folding is the desired behavior. It delegates the date filters to the source so only the needed data for each partition is retrieved, which reduces refresh time and resource usage rather than causing resource exhaustion.

  • Official documentation: Query folding in Power Query

B. Only refresh complete days is selected.

Why it is incorrect: Only refresh complete days is an incremental refresh policy option that makes refreshes ignore the current partial day so results are consistent. It does not increase the amount of data loaded in a way that would exhaust resources; it is not a documented cause of this failure.

  • Official documentation: Incremental refresh for semantic models in Power BI

C. XMLA Endpoint is set to Read Only.

Why it is incorrect: A read-only XMLA endpoint prevents write operations through external tools (such as advanced refresh or deploying metadata). It does not make a scheduled or on-demand refresh run out of resources, and the standard refresh does not depend on external-tool write access.

  • Official documentation: Semantic model connectivity with the XMLA endpoint

E. The delta type of the column used to partition the data has changed.

Why it is incorrect: A change in the data type of the date/time column used for partitioning would cause a schema or type error (or an invalid filter), not a gradual resource exhaustion. The documented cause of "running out of resources" in incremental refresh is the absence of query folding.

  • Official documentation: Troubleshoot incremental refresh and real-time data

q027.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that uses a Microsoft Power BI Premium capacity.

You need to enable scale-out for a semantic model.

What should you do first?
options: At the semantic model level, set Large dataset storage format to Off.
At the tenant level, set Create and use Metrics to Enabled.
At the semantic model level, set Large dataset storage format to On.
At the tenant level, set Data Activator to Enabled.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: At the semantic model level, set Large dataset storage format to On.

Why it is correct: Semantic model scale-out (query scale-out) distributes read-only replicas of a model so that many concurrent users can query it. The configuration procedure in the documentation has a prerequisite: the semantic model must use the Large semantic model storage format, which you enable in the model settings in the Power BI service. Only after that can you turn on scale-out (in the service or through the REST API by setting maxReadOnlyReplicas). Since the question asks what to do first, enabling the large storage format on the semantic model is the answer.

  • Official documentation: Configure semantic model scale-out and Power BI semantic model scale-out
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. At the semantic model level, set Large dataset storage format to Off.

Why it is incorrect: Scale-out requires the large storage format to be enabled, so turning it off is the opposite of what the configuration steps require.

  • Official documentation: Configure semantic model scale-out

B. At the tenant level, set Create and use Metrics to Enabled.

Why it is incorrect: Create and use Metrics is the tenant setting for Power BI goals/scorecards. It is unrelated to semantic model replicas or scale-out.

  • Official documentation: Tenant settings index - Microsoft Fabric

D. At the tenant level, set Data Activator to Enabled.

Why it is incorrect: Data Activator (Fabric Activator) is the tenant setting for event-driven triggers and alerts on data. It has no relationship to scale-out of a semantic model.

  • Official documentation: Tenant settings index - Microsoft Fabric

q028.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a warehouse. The warehouse uses row- level security (RLS).

You create a Direct Lake semantic model that uses the Delta tables and RLS of the warehouse.

When users interact with a report built from the model, which mode will be used by the DAX queries?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: DirectQuery

Why it is correct: even though the semantic model was originally created in Direct Lake mode, Direct Lake models read data straight from the Parquet/Delta files in OneLake without going through the warehouse's SQL engine. Since row-level security (RLS) is defined in the warehouse (at the SQL endpoint level) and not in the semantic model itself, Direct Lake cannot apply those SQL rules directly on the Delta files in OneLake. As a result, whenever a user interacts with a report, the model falls back to DirectQuery against the warehouse's SQL analytics endpoint so that it evaluates and enforces the source RLS before returning the data.

Official documentation: Direct Lake overview - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Dual — Why it is incorrect: Dual is a table storage mode used in traditional composite models (combining Import and DirectQuery for dimension tables), not a query execution mode a Direct Lake model falls back to when RLS exists in the source warehouse. Official documentation: Storage mode in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn
  • Option C — Direct Lake — Why it is incorrect: Direct Lake is only used when Delta tables can be read directly from OneLake without SQL restrictions at the source. When row-level security (RLS) or object/column-level security (OLS) is configured in the source warehouse or SQL endpoint (and not redefined in the semantic model itself), Direct Lake automatically falls back to DirectQuery (or fails if the behavior is locked to Direct Lake only). Official documentation: Direct Lake overview - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — Import — Why it is incorrect: a Direct Lake model never turns its queries into Import mode in real time while a user interacts with a report; in Import mode, data is copied into memory beforehand through a scheduled or manual refresh. Official documentation: Semantic model modes in the Power BI service - Microsoft Learn

Storage mode in Power BI Desktop

q029.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a complex semantic model. The model is based on a star schema and contains many tables, including a fact table named Sales.

You need to create a diagram of the model. The diagram must contain only the Sales table and related tables.

What should you use from Microsoft Power BI Desktop?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Model view

Why it is correct: In Power BI Desktop, Model view (modeling view) shows the tables and relationships of the semantic model as a diagram. In it you can create additional layouts (diagram tabs) and drag in just the tables you need; with the Add related tables option on a table (for example Sales), Desktop adds the fact table and every table directly related to it to that layout. This gives a focused star-schema diagram of Sales and its dimensions, without the other tables of a complex model.

  • Official documentation: Work with Modeling view in Power BI Desktop
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. data categories

Why it is incorrect: Data categories are column properties (for example City, Country or Web URL) that tell Power BI how to treat the data in visuals. They do not produce a diagram of tables.

  • Official documentation: Work with Modeling view in Power BI Desktop

B. Data view

Why it is incorrect: Data view shows the rows and columns of a single table as a grid for inspection. It does not display relationships or let you build a diagram of related tables.

  • Official documentation: Work with Modeling view in Power BI Desktop

D. DAX query view

Why it is incorrect: DAX query view is an editor for writing and running DAX queries (and DAX scripts) against the model. It returns result tables, not a visual diagram of tables and relationships.

  • Official documentation: Work with Modeling view in Power BI Desktop

q030.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a semantic model. The model uses Direct Lake mode.

You suspect that some DAX queries load unnecessary columns into memory.

You need to identify the frequently used columns that are loaded into memory.

What are two ways to achieve the goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
options: Use the Analyze in Excel feature.
Query the DISCOVER_MEMORYGRANT dynamic management view (DMV).

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option B: Use the Vertipaq Analyzer tool.
  • Option C: Query the $System.DISCOVER_STORAGE_TABLE_COLUMN_SEGMENTS dynamic management view (DMV).

Why they are correct: in Direct Lake semantic models, the columns of Delta tables are loaded on demand (transcoding / paging in) from OneLake into the VertiPaq engine's memory as DAX queries require them, and they can stay resident or be evicted depending on usage frequency and memory pressure. To audit exactly which columns are loaded in memory, their size and their activity/temperature:

  • Option B — Vertipaq Analyzer: built into DAX Studio and Tabular Editor, it analyzes the model's internal storage metadata (connected through the XMLA endpoint) and shows each table and column in detail: memory consumption (Dictionary, Data, Hierarchy), cardinality and, specifically in Direct Lake models, residency and temperature metrics (Temperature / Last Accessed), making it possible to spot unnecessary or frequently used columns loaded in RAM.
  • Option C — $System.DISCOVER_STORAGE_TABLE_COLUMN_SEGMENTS: this Analysis Services / tabular engine dynamic management view returns segment-level information about every column stored in the VertiPaq engine, including the in-memory paging state (IS_RESIDENT, i.e. whether the segment is currently loaded in RAM or paged out), segment sizes and column access/temperature statistics in Direct Lake models.

Official documentation: Analyze query processing for Direct Lake semantic models - Microsoft Learn | Use Dynamic Management Views (DMVs) to monitor Analysis Services - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Use the Analyze in Excel feature — Why it is incorrect: Analyze in Excel creates a PivotTable in Excel connected to the semantic model to explore business data through MDX/DAX queries, but it does not expose internal VertiPaq engine diagnostics about memory consumption or which individual columns are loaded in RAM. Official documentation: Analyze in Excel - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — Query the DISCOVER_MEMORYGRANT DMV — Why it is incorrect: DISCOVER_MEMORYGRANT shows the memory grants assigned to active sessions and queries at a given moment (how much memory a query reserved while running), but it gives no per-column breakdown of the model's data and does not identify which columns are loaded in memory or how often they are used. Official documentation: Use Dynamic Management Views (DMVs) to monitor Analysis Services - Microsoft Learn

q031.stem:
You have the source data model shown in the following exhibit.

The primary keys of the tables are indicated by a key symbol beside the columns involved in each key.

You need to create a dimensional data model that will enable the analysis of order items by date, product, and customer.

What should you include in the solution? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • The relationship between OrderItem and Product must be based on: Both the CompanyID and the ProductID columns
  • The Company entity must be: Denormalized into the Customer and Product entities

Why it is correct: Analysis of "The relationship between OrderItem and Product must be based on": In the source model the primary key of Product is the composite key (CompanyID, ProductID), so ProductID alone is not unique: two companies can use the same ProductID for different products. OrderItem carries both CompanyID and ProductID, and a relationship (a foreign key) must reference the complete primary key of the target, not part of it.

  • The relationship between OrderItem and Product must be based on, Both the CompanyID and the ProductID columns: Product's primary key is composite (CompanyID, ProductID); the relationship must reference the full key to identify a single product row per order line.
  • The Company entity must be, Denormalized into the Customer and Product entities: in a star schema dimensions are denormalized: Company's attributes are copied into Customer and Product, removing the Company table and the snowflake.

Incorrect options:

  • The relationship between OrderItem and Product must be based on, The ProductID column — Why it is incorrect: it references only part of a composite key; ProductID repeats across companies and the relationship would be many-to-many, producing wrong totals.
  • The relationship between OrderItem and Product must be based on, A new key that combines the CompanyID and ProductID columns — Why it is incorrect: a surrogate key is a legitimate technique, but the existing keys already identify the product and the exam expects the direct relationship on both columns.
  • The Company entity must be, Omitted — Why it is incorrect: omitting it would lose its attributes and CompanyID would still be needed because it is part of the product and customer keys.
  • The Company entity must be, Denormalized into the Product entity only — Why it is incorrect: Customer also depends on Company; flattening only Product would leave Customer snowflaked and the model would not be a true star.
  • Official documentation: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, Dimensional modeling in Microsoft Fabric Warehouse

links.t: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI
Dimensional modeling in Microsoft Fabric Warehouse

q032.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a semantic model named Model1. Model1 uses Import mode. Model1 contains a table named Orders. Orders has 100 million rows and the following fields.

You need to reduce the memory used by Model1 and the time it takes to refresh the model.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
options: Split OrderDateTime into separate date and time columns.
Replace TotalQuantity with a calculated column.
Convert Quantity into the Text data type.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: Split OrderDateTime into separate date and time columns.
  • Option D: Replace TotalSalesAmount with a measure.

Why they are correct:

  • Option A — Split OrderDateTime into separate date and time columns: in a 100-million-row table, a combined Date/Time column has a very high cardinality (millions of unique timestamps down to the second), which forces the VertiPaq columnar storage engine to build a giant dictionary and compresses segments poorly. Splitting OrderDateTime into a Date column (only ~365 distinct values per year) and a Time column (at most 86,400 seconds per day) drastically lowers the cardinality of both columns, massively reducing RAM use and speeding up compression during model refresh. Official documentation: Data reduction techniques for Import modeling - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — Replace TotalSalesAmount with a measure: TotalSalesAmount is currently a calculated column (Quantity * Price) materialized in a 100-million-row table. DAX calculated columns are recomputed row by row on every model refresh (increasing refresh time), occupy physical RAM (with high decimal cardinality) and do not compress as efficiently as imported columns. Replacing it with a DAX measure (SUMX(Orders, Orders[Quantity] * Orders[Price])) evaluates the calculation dynamically only at query time over aggregated data, completely removing its memory footprint and its calculation cost during refresh. Official documentation: Data reduction techniques for Import modeling - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B — Replace TotalQuantity with a calculated column — Why it is incorrect: TotalQuantity is already correctly defined as a measure (which consumes no memory or refresh time). Turning it into a calculated column in a 100-million-row table would produce exactly the opposite of the desired effect: it would increase RAM usage and lengthen refresh time. Official documentation: Calculated columns in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn
  • Option C — Convert Quantity to the Text data type — Why it is incorrect: in the VertiPaq engine, integer numeric types use Value Encoding, which is much more compact and fast than the Hash (dictionary) Encoding used for string columns. Converting an integer to text increases memory use and degrades aggregation performance. Official documentation: Data reduction techniques for Import modeling - Microsoft Learn

links.t: Data reduction techniques for Import modeling
Calculated columns in Power BI Desktop

q033.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a semantic model.

You need to prevent report creators from populating visuals by using implicit measures.

What are two tools that you can use to achieve the goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: Microsoft Power BI Desktop
  • Option B: Tabular Editor

Why they are correct: to prevent report creators from adding columns directly to visuals (creating implicit measures), you must enable the tabular model property Discourage implicit measures (set to True).

  • Option A — Microsoft Power BI Desktop: Power BI Desktop lets you change the Discourage implicit measures property directly in Model view: select the semantic model's root node in the Data pane (or the Model tab of the model explorer) and turn on the Discourage implicit measures switch in the Properties pane. (Creating any calculation group in Power BI Desktop also turns this property on automatically.) Official documentation: Model explorer in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn | Calculation groups in Power BI - Microsoft Learn
  • Option B — Tabular Editor: connected locally to a .pbix/.pbip file or remotely to the Fabric workspace through the XMLA endpoint, Tabular Editor exposes all the TOM (Tabular Object Model) properties of the Model object. Selecting the Model node in the object tree and setting Discourage Implicit Measures to True disables implicit measures in reports connected to the model. Official documentation: Model.DiscourageImplicitMeasures Property (Tabular Object Model) - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option C — Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) — Why it is incorrect: although SSMS can connect to a semantic model's XMLA endpoint to query data, browse objects or run manual TMSL scripts, it does not provide a graphical tabular-model properties interface to edit DiscourageImplicitMeasures as a modeling tool, unlike Power BI Desktop and Tabular Editor. Official documentation: Semantic model connectivity with the XMLA endpoint - Microsoft Learn
  • Option D — DAX Studio — Why it is incorrect: DAX Studio is a DAX query execution and diagnostic tool (server timings, query plans and VertiPaq Analyzer), but it does not edit semantic model metadata or properties. Official documentation: External tools in Power BI Desktop - Microsoft Learn

q034.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains two lakehouses.

You are building a dataflow that will combine data from the lakehouses. The applied steps from one of the queries in the dataflow is shown in the following exhibit.

Use the drop-down menus to select the answer choice that completes each statement based on the information presented in the graphic.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • [Answer choice] of the transformation steps in the query will fold: Some
  • The Added custom step will be performed in: the Microsoft Power Query engine

Why it is correct: Analysis of the first statement: The Applied steps pane shows query folding indicators next to each step. The first steps (Source, Navigation) show the indicator that means the step folds, that is, it is translated into a query evaluated by the data source. The "Capitalized each word" step shows an indicator that is different (orange/red), which signals that folding stops there: that step and the ones after it are not pushed to the source. Because some steps fold and others do not, the answer is Some.

  • [Answer choice] of the transformation steps in the query will fold, Some: the first steps (Source, Navigation) fold, but the 'Capitalized each word' step breaks folding: some steps fold and others do not.
  • The Added custom step will be performed in, the Microsoft Power Query engine: after a step that breaks folding, the following ones (including Added custom) are evaluated locally in the Microsoft Power Query engine.

Incorrect options:

  • [Answer choice] of the transformation steps in the query will fold, All — Why it is incorrect: the indicators show steps that do not fold and the 'View data source query' options are greyed out: not all of them fold.
  • [Answer choice] of the transformation steps in the query will fold, None — Why it is incorrect: the initial steps (Source and Navigation) do fold, so it is not true that nothing folds.
  • The Added custom step will be performed in, each lakehouse's query engine — Why it is incorrect: each lakehouse only runs what folded into the query it receives; the step after the break is not sent and the query also combines two lakehouses.
  • The Added custom step will be performed in, the source lakehouse query engine — Why it is incorrect: the source lakehouse only evaluates the folded part, not the steps after the break.
  • Official documentation: Query folding indicators, Overview of query evaluation and query folding in Power Query

q035.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse’.

Lakehouse1 contains a table named Tablet.

You are creating a new data pipeline.

You plan to copy external data to Table’. The schema of the external data changes regularly.

You need the copy operation to meet the following requirements:

Replace Table1 with the schema of the external data.

Replace all the data in Table1 with the rows in the external data.

You add a Copy data activity to the pipeline.

What should you do for the Copy data activity?
options: From the Source tab, add additional columns.
From the Destination tab, set Table action to Overwrite.
From the Settings tab, select Enable staging.
From the Source tab, select Enable partition discovery.
From the Source tab, select Recursively.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: From the Destination tab, set Table action to Overwrite.

Why it is correct: The two requirements are to replace the schema of Table1 with the schema of the external data and to replace all the rows. For a Lakehouse table destination, the Copy data activity offers the Table action setting. Overwrite "overwrites the existing data and schema in the table using the new values", which meets both requirements, even when the source schema changes regularly. With Append the old rows would be kept and the existing schema would not be replaced.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. From the Source tab, add additional columns.

Why it is incorrect: Additional columns add extra fields (such as a file path or a static value) to the data copied from the source. This does not control whether the destination table is replaced or appended to.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity

C. From the Settings tab, select Enable staging.

Why it is incorrect: Staging uses an intermediate storage location to improve performance for some copy scenarios. It does not define how the destination table is written, so it does not replace the schema or the data.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity

D. From the Source tab, select Enable partition discovery.

Why it is incorrect: Partition discovery makes the source read partition information from the folder structure of file-based sources (for example year=2024/month=01) and expose it as columns. It is a read-side feature and has no effect on replacing the destination table.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity

E. From the Source tab, select Recursively.

Why it is incorrect: Recursively only controls whether the copy reads files from subfolders of the source folder. It does not change how the destination is written.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity

q036.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse.

You plan to query sales data files by using the SQL endpoint. The files will be in an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) storage bucket.

You need to recommend which file format to use and where to create a shortcut.

Which two actions should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
options: Create a shortcut in the Files section.
Create a shortcut in the Tables section.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option D: Create a shortcut in the Tables section.
  • Option E: Use the delta format.

Why they are correct: to query with T-SQL, through a Fabric lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint, data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket without duplicating or ingesting it first, two architectural conditions are required:

  • Option D — Create a shortcut in the Tables section: a lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint only automatically exposes objects located in the Tables section (not files in Files). When you create a OneLake shortcut to Amazon S3 directly in the Tables section, Fabric mounts it as a virtual table in the metastore and makes it immediately queryable with T-SQL. Official documentation: OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Learn | Create an Amazon S3 shortcut - Microsoft Learn
  • Option E — Use the delta format: for a shortcut created in the Tables section to be recognized as a valid table and queried automatically by the SQL analytics endpoint's T-SQL engine (and by Direct Lake), the target data in Amazon S3 must follow the Delta Lake format (Parquet files plus their _delta_log transaction log folder). If the folder pointed to in Tables is not Delta, the SQL endpoint will not expose it as a queryable table (it shows as an unidentified table or unsupported folder). Official documentation: Lakehouse and Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn | SQL analytics endpoint of the lakehouse - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option A — Create a shortcut in the Files section — Why it is incorrect: shortcuts created in the Files section are treated as unstructured storage accessible through Spark, Python or Dataflows, but they do not appear as tables in the SQL analytics endpoint, so they cannot be queried directly with T-SQL in the lakehouse's SQL endpoint. Official documentation: Explore the data in your lakehouse - Microsoft Learn
  • Option B — Use the Parquet format — Why it is incorrect: although Delta Lake stores its underlying data in Parquet files, plain Parquet files on their own (without the Delta _delta_log transaction log) are not automatically registered or recognized as managed/virtual tables in the Tables section for the lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint. Official documentation: Lakehouse and Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
  • Option C — Use the CSV format — Why it is incorrect: CSV is a non-transactional plain-text format that cannot be exposed directly as a native table in the Tables section to be queried through the SQL analytics endpoint without first converting it to Delta format. Official documentation: Lakehouse and Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn

q037.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

Lakehouse1 contains a subfolder named Subfolder1 that contains CSV files.

You need to convert the CSV files into the delta format that has V-Order optimization enabled.

What should you do from Lakehouse explorer?
options: Use the Load to Tables feature.
Create a new shortcut in the Files section.
Create a new shortcut in the Tables section.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Use the Load to Tables feature.

Why it is correct: In Lakehouse explorer, you can right-click a folder or file in the Files section and choose Load to Tables. The feature converts CSV (or Parquet) files into a Delta table, and tables loaded this way are always in the Delta Lake format with V-Order optimization enabled. It therefore meets both requirements (conversion to Delta and V-Order) in a single action, without writing code.

  • Official documentation: Load to Delta Lake tables
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

B. Create a new shortcut in the Files section.

Why it is incorrect: A shortcut only creates a pointer to existing data. It does not convert anything: the CSV files stay CSV.

  • Official documentation: Lakehouse shortcuts

C. Create a new shortcut in the Tables section.

Why it is incorrect: A Tables-section shortcut also only references existing data, and it is recognized as a table only if the target is already in Delta format. It does not convert CSV into Delta and does not apply V-Order.

  • Official documentation: Lakehouse shortcuts

D. Use the Optimize feature.

Why it is incorrect: Table maintenance (Optimize) compacts small files and can apply V-Order, but only on tables that already are Delta. It cannot turn a folder of CSV files into a Delta table.

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake table optimization and V-Order

q038.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

Lakehouse1 contains an unpartitioned table named Table1.

You plan to copy data to Table1 and partition the table based on a date column in the source data.

You create a Copy activity to copy the data to Table1.

You need to specify the partition column in the Destination settings of the Copy activity.

What should you do first?
options: From the Destination tab, set Mode to Append.
From the Destination tab, select the partition column.
From the Source tab, select Enable partition discovery.
From the Destination tabs, set Mode to Overwrite.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: From the Destination tabs, set Mode to Overwrite.

Why it is correct: Partitioning is configured in the Advanced options of the Lakehouse table destination of the Copy activity (Enable Partition, then Partition column name). Since Table1 already exists and is unpartitioned, the partition layout can only be applied by rewriting the table, and that is what Overwrite does (it replaces the data and the schema). The first thing to do is therefore to set the table action to Overwrite; once that is set, you can enable partitioning and select the date column in the destination columns. When you append to an existing table, the partition columns are derived from the existing table, so an unpartitioned table cannot be partitioned with Append.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity and Load data to Lakehouse using partition in a data pipeline
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. From the Destination tab, set Mode to Append.

Why it is incorrect: With Append on an existing table, the partition columns are taken from the existing table, which is unpartitioned, so you cannot introduce a new partitioning scheme this way. The existing data would also remain unpartitioned.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity

B. From the Destination tab, select the partition column.

Why it is incorrect: This is the step you want to reach, but not the first one: the partition options depend on the table action, and for an existing unpartitioned table you must first choose Overwrite. The question asks what to do first.

  • Official documentation: Load data to Lakehouse using partition in a data pipeline

C. From the Source tab, select Enable partition discovery.

Why it is incorrect: Partition discovery is a source-side setting that reads partition folders of file-based sources as columns. It does not define how the destination table is partitioned.

  • Official documentation: Configure Lakehouse in a copy activity

q039.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1.

Warehouse1 contains a fact table named FactSales that has one billion rows.

You run the following T-SQL statement.

CREATE TABLE test.FactSales AS CLONE OF Dbo.FactSales;

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true.

Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • A replica of dbo.Sales is created in the test schema by copying the metadata only: Yes
  • Additional schema changes to dbo.FactSales will also apply to test.FactSales (first occurrence): No
  • Additional schema changes to dbo.FactSales will also apply to test.FactSales (second occurrence): No

Analysis of statement 1 (Yes): CREATE TABLE test.FactSales AS CLONE OF dbo.FactSales creates a zero-copy clone in Fabric Warehouse. Only the metadata of the source table is copied, and the clone points to the same underlying Parquet files in OneLake, so a table of one billion rows is cloned almost instantly with no data duplication. (The statement names dbo.Sales instead of dbo.FactSales, which is a typo in the question; the intended meaning is that the replica is created in the test schema by copying metadata only, so the answer is Yes.)

  • Official documentation: Clone table in Microsoft Fabric

Analysis of statements 2 and 3 (No, No): Both statements are identical. A clone is an independent table: after it is created, changes made to the source (including schema changes, data changes and later schema evolution) are not propagated to the clone, and changes to the clone are not reflected in the source. The two tables only share the original data files until either one is modified, at which point the modified table writes its own new files.

  • Official documentation: Clone table in Microsoft Fabric

q040.stem:
You have source data in a folder on a local computer.

You need to create a solution that will use Fabric to populate a data store. The solution must meet the following requirements:

Support the use of dataflows to load and append data to the data store.

Ensure that Delta tables are V-Order optimized and compacted automatically.

Which type of data store should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: a lakehouse

Why it is correct: The requirements are to use dataflows to load and append data, and to have Delta tables that are V-Order optimized and compacted automatically. A lakehouse stores its tables in Delta format, is a supported destination for Dataflow Gen2 (with Append or Replace as the update method), and the Spark engine writes Delta tables with V-Order and the lakehouse supports automatic table maintenance such as compaction. A dataflow can also read files from a local folder, so the source data can be uploaded and loaded.

  • Official documentation: Dataflow Gen2 data destinations and managed settings and Delta Lake table optimization and V-Order
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

B. an Azure SQL database

Why it is incorrect: An Azure SQL database is not a Fabric item that stores Delta tables, so the Delta V-Order and automatic compaction requirements do not apply to it. It stores data in its own relational format.

  • Official documentation: Dataflow Gen2 data destinations and managed settings

C. a warehouse

Why it is incorrect: A warehouse also stores its data as Delta in OneLake and applies V-Order, but the requirement describes Delta tables that you manage and that are compacted automatically in the lakehouse scenario with dataflows loading and appending data. The comparison the exam intends is that lakehouse is the store that fits dataflows plus Delta table optimization, while a warehouse is a T-SQL-centric engine.

  • Official documentation: Understand V-Order for Microsoft Fabric Warehouse

D. a KQL database

Why it is incorrect: A KQL database (in an eventhouse) is designed for real-time and time-series data queried with KQL, and its storage is not managed as V-Order Delta tables for dataflow-based loading in this scenario.

  • Official documentation: Dataflow Gen2 data destinations and managed settings

q041.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse.

You are using a Fabric notebook to save a large DataFrame by using the following code. df.write.partitionBy(“year”, “month”,

“day”).mode(“overwrite”).parquet(“Files/SalesOrder”)

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true.

Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Statement 1 - The results will form a hierarchy of folders for each partition key: Yes
  • Statement 2 - The resulting file partitions can be read in parallel across multiple nodes: Yes
  • Statement 3 - The resulting file partitions will use file compression: No

Statement 1 (Yes). partitionBy("year", "month", "day") makes Spark write the data in a Hive-style directory layout, one nested level per partition column and in the order given: Files/SalesOrder/year=2024/month=5/day=17/part-....parquet. The result is therefore a hierarchy of folders (year, then month, then day). The alternative "No" is wrong because partitioning is precisely what creates that folder tree; without partitionBy all part files would sit directly under Files/SalesOrder. Note also that the target is the Files section of the lakehouse, so the output is plain Parquet files (unmanaged), not a Delta table.

  • Official documentation: partitionBy (DataFrameWriter) and Load data into your lakehouse with a notebook - Microsoft Fabric

Statement 2 (Yes). The write produces many independent Parquet part files spread across the partition folders. Spark distributes the read of those files as tasks across the executors (nodes) of the Spark pool, and a later query that filters on year, month or day can also skip entire folders (partition pruning). Parquet is a splittable, columnar format, so parallel reads across nodes are the normal behavior. "No" would only be true for a single non-splittable file read by one task, which is not this case.

  • Official documentation: Read and write Parquet files

Statement 3 (No). The statement says that the file partitions "will use file compression" as a consequence of this code. The code does not configure any compression option, so nothing in this write explicitly enables it. The point of the item is that compression is a property of the file format/codec setting, not something that partitionBy or mode("overwrite") provides.

⚠️ Heads-up: The study source marks this answer, but Spark's default Parquet codec (snappy) does compress the pages inside each file, so "Yes" could also be argued for this statement. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Read and write Parquet files

q042.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a data flow named Dataflow1 contains a query that returns the data shown in the following exhibit.

You need to transform the data columns into attribute-value pairs, where columns become rows.

You select the VendorID column.

Which transformation should you select from the context menu of the VendorID column?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Unpivot other columns

Why it is correct: The exhibit shows a wide table: one VendorID column followed by one column per date (2015-01-01, 2015-01-02, ...). To turn the date columns into rows you need attribute-value pairs, where the attribute column holds the former column names (the dates) and the value column holds the numbers. Because you selected only VendorID (the column that must stay as an identifier), the right command is Unpivot other columns: it keeps the selected column(s) as they are and unpivots every other column, including date columns that might be added later (it generates Table.UnpivotOtherColumns). The result has the columns VendorID, Attribute, Value.

  • Official documentation: Unpivot columns - Power Query and Table.UnpivotOtherColumns - PowerQuery M
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Group by

Why it is incorrect: Group by aggregates rows (sum, count, etc.) by one or more key columns. It reduces the number of rows and does not convert column headers into rows.

  • Official documentation: Unpivot columns - Power Query

B. Unpivot columns

Why it is incorrect: "Unpivot columns" unpivots only the columns that are selected. Since the selected column is VendorID, it would unpivot that single column and leave all the date columns as columns, which is the opposite of what is needed. You would have to select all the date columns instead, and the step would not pick up new date columns automatically.

  • Official documentation: Unpivot columns - Power Query

D. Split column

Why it is incorrect: Split column divides the contents of a column into several columns (by delimiter, number of characters, etc.). It does not rotate columns into rows.

  • Official documentation: Unpivot columns - Power Query

E. Remove other columns

Why it is incorrect: It deletes every column except the selected one, so you would keep only VendorID and lose all the data. It is a projection, not a reshape.

  • Official documentation: Unpivot columns - Power Query

q043.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a data pipeline.

You need to ensure that the pipeline runs every four hours on Mondays and Fridays.

To what should you set Repeat for the schedule?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Hourly

Why it is correct: The Hourly repeat option lets you run the pipeline every N hours (1 to 72), so "every four hours" is a native setting of this option.

⚠️ Heads-up: The study source marks this answer, but the scenario also requires running only on Mondays and Fridays, and in the Fabric scheduler selecting specific weekdays is available only with the Weekly repeat option (where you pick the days and add run times such as 00:00, 04:00, 08:00, 12:00, 16:00 and 20:00). The Hourly option exposes only an interval, so by itself it would run every day, which makes C (Weekly) arguable. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Job Scheduler in Microsoft Fabric and Run, schedule, or use events to trigger a pipeline
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Daily

Why it is incorrect: Daily schedules run every day (with up to a few run times) and have no weekday selection, so they cannot be restricted to Monday and Friday.

  • Official documentation: Job Scheduler in Microsoft Fabric

B. By the minute

Why it is incorrect: Minute-based schedules repeat every 1 to 720 minutes. Four hours is 240 minutes, so the interval would fit, but the option has no weekday filter and would run all seven days.

  • Official documentation: Job Scheduler in Microsoft Fabric

C. Weekly

Why it is incorrect: It is not the expected answer for this question, although Weekly is the only option that lets you choose Monday and Friday and add several times of day (every four hours), which is why it could be argued in practice.

q044.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a warehouse.

Several times a day, the performance of all warehouse queries degrades. You suspect that Fabric is throttling the compute used by the warehouse.

What should you use to identify whether throttling is occurring?
options: the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app

Why it is correct: Warehouse queries consume capacity units (CU) from the Fabric capacity. When usage exceeds the purchased capacity, Fabric first smooths the load and then applies throttling (delays or rejections) to interactive operations, which shows up as periodic slowdowns of every query. The tool built to see this is the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app: its Compute page and the throttling/overage views show CU utilization over time, background and interactive smoothing, and when the capacity entered throttling states. Matching the times of the slowdowns with those charts confirms or rules out throttling for the warehouse.

  • Official documentation: Understand capacity throttling and smoothing, Capacity Metrics app compute page and Monitoring scenarios in the Capacity Metrics app
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. the Capacity settings

Why it is incorrect: The capacity settings in the admin portal let you configure a capacity (size, notifications, workload settings, delegation). They are not a monitoring tool and do not show historical utilization or throttling events.

  • Official documentation: Understand capacity throttling and smoothing

B. the Monitoring hub

Why it is incorrect: The Monitoring hub lists the activities and their status (running, failed, duration) for Fabric items, such as pipeline runs and refreshes. It does not report capacity-level CU consumption or throttling state.

  • Official documentation: Monitoring scenarios in the Capacity Metrics app

C. dynamic management views (DMVs)

Why it is incorrect: DMVs show live connections, sessions and requests inside the warehouse (for example, which query is running or blocked), not whether the capacity is throttling. A query being slow because of throttling would look just like any other slow query in a DMV.

  • Official documentation: Monitor connections, sessions, and requests using DMVs

q045.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that uses the default Spark starter pool and runtime version 1.2.

You plan to read a CSV file named Sales_raw.csv in a lakehouse, select columns, and save the data as a Delta table to the managed area of the lakehouse.

Sales_raw.csv contains 12 columns.

You have the following code.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true.

Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Statement 1 - The Spark engine will read only the SalesOrderNumber, OrderDate, CustomerName and UnitPrice columns from Sales_raw.csv: Yes
  • Statement 2 - Removing the partition will reduce the execution time of the query: No
  • Statement 3 - Adding inferSchema='true' to the options will increase the execution time of the query: Yes

Statement 1 (Yes). Spark evaluates lazily: the select(...) that follows load(...) is folded by the Catalyst optimizer into the file scan, so only the four columns needed (plus OrderDate, which feeds Year) are materialized from the 12-column CSV. This column pruning applies to the CSV data source too. The objection that a CSV text file must be read entirely is true at the I/O level, because each line must be scanned, but the engine parses and keeps only the required columns.

  • Official documentation: Load data into your lakehouse with a notebook - Microsoft Fabric

Statement 2 (No). The partition (partitionBy('Year')) only affects the write phase: it creates one folder per year in the managed sales Delta table. With a low-cardinality column such as year it adds negligible overhead, and the cost of the job is dominated by reading and parsing the CSV, which does not change when you remove it. Removing it therefore does not meaningfully reduce execution time (and it would hurt later queries that filter by year).

  • Official documentation: Delta Lake table optimization and V-Order and Tune file size

Statement 3 (Yes). With inferSchema set to true, Spark has to make an additional pass over the CSV file to sample the values and infer the type of every column before the real read. That extra scan increases the execution time compared with using the default (all columns as strings) or an explicit schema, which is the recommended approach for large files.

  • Official documentation: Load data into your lakehouse with a notebook - Microsoft Fabric

q046.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a warehouse.

A user discovers that a report that usually takes two minutes to render has been running for 45 minutes and has still not rendered.

You need to identify what is preventing the report query from completing.

Which dynamic management view (DMV) should you use?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: sys.dm_exec_requests

Why it is correct: The report query has been running for 45 minutes and you need to know what is holding it back. sys.dm_exec_requests returns one row per request that is currently executing in the warehouse, including its status, start_time, total_elapsed_time, and the wait information (wait_type, wait_time, blocking_session_id), so you can see whether the request is suspended, waiting or blocked. In Fabric Data Warehouse the documented DMVs are sys.dm_exec_connections, sys.dm_exec_sessions and sys.dm_exec_requests; you join them (by session_id) to get the login and the SQL text of the running statement.

  • Official documentation: Monitor connections, sessions, and requests using DMVs - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

B. sys.dm_exec_sessions

Why it is incorrect: It describes authenticated sessions (login, host, program, status, last request time), but not the execution state of the query or what it is waiting on. It helps to identify who is connected, not what blocks the request.

  • Official documentation: Monitor connections, sessions, and requests using DMVs - Microsoft Fabric

C. sys.dm_exec_connections

Why it is incorrect: It shows connection-level information (client address, protocol, encryption, bytes read and written). It has no per-query status or wait data, so it cannot tell you why a statement is not finishing. It is the least useful of the three for this purpose.

  • Official documentation: sys.dm_exec_connections (Transact-SQL)

D. sys.dm_pdw_exec_requests

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • First box (object before the dot): Value
  • Second box (function after the dot): NativeQuery
  • Third box (record field set to true): EnableFolding

Why it is correct: The completed code is Query = Value.NativeQuery(Database, "SELECT * FROM customer WHERE country IN ('USA', 'UK')", null, [EnableFolding = true]).

  • First box (object before the dot), Value: the function that sends a native statement to the source is Value.NativeQuery, from the Value library.

  • Third box (record field set to true), EnableFolding: [EnableFolding = true] tells Power Query that the following foldable steps can be delegated to the SQL Server engine.

Incorrect options:

  • First box (object before the dot), EnableFolding — Why it is incorrect: EnableFolding is a field of the options record, not a function library.
  • First box (object before the dot), NativeQuery — Why it is incorrect: NativeQuery is the function name, not the object before the dot.

  • Second box (function after the dot), Table — Why it is incorrect: Table is a data type/library, not the function name.

q048.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

Readings from 100 IoT devices are appended to a Delta table in Lakehouse1.

Each set of readings is approximately 25 KB. Approximately 10 GB of data is received daily.

All the table and SparkSession settings are set to the default.

You discover that queries are slow to execute. In addition, the lakehouse storage contains data and log files that are no longer used.

You need to remove the files that are no longer used and combine small files into larger files with a target size of 1 GB per file.

What should you do? To answer, drag the appropriate actions to the correct requirements. Each action may be used once, more than once, or not at all. You may need to drag the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Remove the files: Run the VACUUM command on a schedule.
  • Combine the files: Run the OPTIMIZE command on a schedule.

Why it is correct: Remove the files (VACUUM). After updates, deletes, overwrites and OPTIMIZE, Delta Lake keeps the previous data files and log entries so that time travel works. They are no longer referenced by the current table version but still occupy storage. VACUUM deletes the data files that are unreferenced and older than the retention threshold (7 days by default). Because the problem states that the storage holds unused data and log files, the action that removes them is VACUUM, and it has to be run (for example from a scheduled notebook or the lakehouse maintenance feature) because it is not automatic. Setting parallelDelete only changes how fast a VACUUM deletes files; it does not remove anything by itself.

  • Remove the files, Run the VACUUM command on a schedule.: after updates, deletes and OPTIMIZE, Delta keeps unreferenced files for time travel; VACUUM removes those older than the retention threshold and must be run on a schedule.
  • Combine the files, Run the OPTIMIZE command on a schedule.: OPTIMIZE bins small Parquet files into larger ones (≈1 GB target); running it on a schedule compacts the files that already exist.

Incorrect options:

  • Remove the files, Set the autoCompact table setting. — Why it is incorrect: The table autoCompact setting compacts newly written files; it does not remove unreferenced files.
  • Remove the files, Set the optimizeWrite table setting. — Why it is incorrect: optimizeWrite improves the size of files being written; it does not remove obsolete files.
  • Remove the files, Set the autoCompact SparkSession setting. — Why it is incorrect: The SparkSession autoCompact setting is preventive for future writes; it does not clean unused files.
  • Remove the files, Run the OPTIMIZE command on a schedule. — Why it is incorrect: OPTIMIZE merges small files, but it does not delete unused data and log files.
  • Remove the files, Set the parallelDelete SparkSession setting. — Why it is incorrect: parallelDelete only speeds up VACUUM; on its own it deletes nothing.
  • Combine the files, Set the autoCompact table setting. — Why it is incorrect: The table autoCompact setting acts on future writes and is not tied to a 1 GB target; it does not compact existing files.
  • Combine the files, Set the optimizeWrite table setting. — Why it is incorrect: optimizeWrite is preventive (improves what is written from now on); it does not merge existing small files.
  • Combine the files, Run the VACUUM command on a schedule. — Why it is incorrect: VACUUM removes unreferenced files; it does not merge small files.
  • Combine the files, Set the autoCompact SparkSession setting. — Why it is incorrect: The SparkSession autoCompact setting only affects future writes and does not guarantee the 1 GB target.
  • Combine the files, Set the parallelDelete SparkSession setting. — Why it is incorrect: parallelDelete only changes the speed of VACUUM; it does not merge files.

q049.stem:
You need to create a data loading pattern for a Type 1 slowly changing dimension (SCD).

Which two actions should you include in the process? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
options: Update rows when the non-key attributes have changed.
Insert new rows when the natural key exists in the dimension table, and the non-key attribute values have changed.
Update the effective end date of rows when the non-key attribute values have changed.
Insert new records when the natural key is a new value in the table.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Update rows when the non-key attributes have changed.
  • Option C: Update the effective end date of rows when the non-key attribute values have changed.

Why it is correct: Option A is the defining behavior of a Type 1 SCD: when a natural key already exists and an attribute changed, the existing row is overwritten, so no history is kept. Option C is the second action accepted for this question: the load also maintains the effective end date of rows whose non-key attribute values changed.

⚠️ Heads-up: The study source marks this answer, but updating an effective end date is part of a Type 2 pattern (the old row is closed and a new current row is inserted), while Type 1 keeps no history. A Type 1 load is usually described as updating changed rows (A) and inserting rows whose natural key is new (D), so A and D could also be argued. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Slowly changing dimension type 1 and Modeling dimension tables in Warehouse
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

B. Insert new rows when the natural key exists in the dimension table, and the non-key attribute values have changed.

Why it is incorrect: Inserting a new version of a row for an existing key preserves history, which is the Type 2 pattern. Type 1 overwrites in place.

  • Official documentation: Load tables in a dimensional model

D. Insert new records when the natural key is a new value in the table.

Why it is incorrect: It is not the expected answer for this question, although inserting rows for natural keys that do not yet exist is a standard part of every SCD load, including Type 1 (an upsert/MERGE: update matched, insert not matched).

  • Official documentation: Slowly changing dimension type 1

q051.stem:
You are analyzing customer purchases in a Fabric notebook by using PySpark.

You have the following DataFrames:

transactions: Contains five columns named transaction_id, customer_id, product_id, amount, and date and has 10 million rows, with each row

representing a transaction. customers: Contains customer details in 1,000 rows and three columns named customer_id, name, and country.

You need to join the DataFrames on the customer_id column. The solution must minimize data shuffling.

You write the following code.

from pyspark.sql import functions as F

results =

Which code should you run to populate the results DataFrame?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: transactions.join(F.broadcast(customers), transactions.customer_id == customers.customer_id)

Why it is correct: The transactions DataFrame is large (10 million rows) while customers is tiny (1,000 rows). With a regular join Spark would normally pick a sort-merge join, which shuffles both sides across the cluster so that rows with the same customer_id end up on the same executor. By wrapping the small DataFrame in F.broadcast(), you tell Spark to use a broadcast hash join: the 1,000 customer rows are copied once to every executor and each executor joins them against its local partitions of transactions. The large table is never repartitioned, so the shuffle of the 10 million rows is avoided, which is exactly the requirement of the scenario ("minimize data shuffling").

  • Official documentation: Join hints (BROADCAST) in Spark SQL and Data processing optimization for Apache Spark
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

B. transactions.join(customers, transactions.customer_id == customers.customer_id).distinct()

Why it is incorrect: This does not influence the join strategy at all, and .distinct() adds an extra wide transformation (another shuffle to deduplicate the whole result). It therefore increases shuffling instead of minimizing it, and it may even remove legitimate duplicate rows.

  • Official documentation: Data processing optimization for Apache Spark

C. transactions.join(customers, transactions.customer_id == customers.customer_id)

Why it is incorrect: It is a valid inner join, but without a hint Spark relies on its automatic choice. Although Spark can auto-broadcast small tables under a size threshold, that depends on statistics and configuration and is not guaranteed; the explicit broadcast() is the way to guarantee that the small side is broadcast and the large side is not shuffled. This option does not explicitly minimize the shuffle, so it is not the best answer.

  • Official documentation: Join hints in Spark SQL

D. transactions.crossJoin(customers).where(transactions.customer_id == customers.customer_id)

Why it is incorrect: A cross join first builds the Cartesian product (10 million x 1,000 = 10 billion rows) and only then filters it. This is extremely expensive in data movement and compute, is the opposite of an optimization and is a classic anti-pattern when an equi-join is what you need.

  • Official documentation: Data processing optimization for Apache Spark

q053.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1.

Lakehouse1 contains a table named Nyctaxi_raw. Nyctaxi_row contains the following table:

You create a Fabric notebook and attach it to Lakehouse1.

You need to use PySpark code to transform the data. The solution must meet the following requirements:

Add a column named pickupDate that will contain only the date portion of pickupDateTime.

Filter the DataFrame to include only rows where fareAmount is a positive number that is less than 100.

How should you complete the code? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Box 1 (the method on df): df.withColumn
  • Box 2 (the conversion): .cast('date')
  • Box 3 (the row filter): .filter("fareAmount > 0 AND fareAmount < 100")

Resulting code:

df = spark.read.format("delta").load("Tables/nyctaxi_raw")
df2 = df.withColumn("pickupDate", df['pickupDateTime'].cast('date')) \
        .filter("fareAmount > 0 AND fareAmount < 100")

Note: the exam screenshot has typos (tpepPickupDateTime and farAmount); this is the only syntactically and logically valid option in the list.

Why they are correct:

  • Box 1 — df.withColumn: the requirement is to add a new column pickupDate while keeping all the other columns. DataFrame.withColumn(colName, col) returns a new DataFrame adding (or replacing) that column and leaving the rest intact. Official documentation: pyspark.sql.DataFrame.withColumn - Apache Spark
  • Box 2 — .cast('date'): the source column is a Timestamp and only the date part is needed. Column.cast('date') drops the time component and returns a Date (YYYY-MM-DD). Official documentation: pyspark.sql.Column.cast - Apache Spark
  • Box 3 — .filter("fareAmount > 0 AND fareAmount < 100"): .filter() accepts a SQL expression string and returns only the rows meeting both conditions (positive and below 100). Official documentation: pyspark.sql.DataFrame.filter - Apache Spark

Incorrect options:

  • Box 1 — df.columns — Why it is incorrect: it is a property (not callable) that returns a Python list of column names; calling it raises a TypeError.
  • Box 1 — df.select — Why it is incorrect: select projects existing columns or expressions; it does not take a (new name, expression) signature and would not keep the other columns.
  • Box 1 — df.withColumnsRenamed — Why it is incorrect: it only renames existing columns using a dictionary {old: new}; it does not create a new column by transforming another.
  • Box 2 — alias('date') — Why it is incorrect: it only assigns a name; it does not convert Timestamp to Date, so the time is kept.
  • Box 2 — cast('pickupDate') — Why it is incorrect: the argument of cast must be a valid Spark SQL type ('date', 'int', 'string'), not the target column name; it raises a ParseException.
  • Box 2 — getfield('date') — Why it is incorrect: the correct method is getField and it extracts a field of a StructType column, not the date of a Timestamp.
  • Box 3 — filter(col('fareAmount').contains('1..100')) — Why it is incorrect: contains looks for a literal substring in string values; it does not evaluate numeric ranges.
  • Box 3 — when(df.fareAmount > 0 AND fareAmount < 100) — Why it is incorrect: when() is a conditional column function, not a row filter; also, Python column expressions need the bitwise & with parentheses, not the keyword AND.
  • Box 3 — where(df.fareAmount.isin((1,100))) — Why it is incorrect: isin only matches values exactly equal to 1 or 100, excluding all values in between (e.g. 15.50).

You need to recommend a solution to prepare the tenant for the PoC.

Which two actions should you recommend performing from the Fabric Admin portal? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options: Enable the Users can try Microsoft Fabric paid features option for the entire organization.
Enable the Users can try Microsoft Fabric paid features option for specific security groups.
Enable the Allow Azure Active Directory guest users to access Microsoft Fabric option for specific security groups.
Enable the Users can create Fabric items option and exclude specific security groups.
Enable the Users can create Fabric items option for specific security groups.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Enable the Users can try Microsoft Fabric paid features option for specific security groups.
  • Option E: Enable the Users can create Fabric items option for specific security groups.

Why it is correct: The Litware case states that Fabric features will be enabled in the existing tenant, that only the analytics team (and the Fabric administrators) may see the PoC items, that the remaining users get access to Fabric features only after the PoC, that the PoC runs on a Fabric trial capacity, and that the principle of least privilege must be followed.

  • Option B: The trial capacity is obtained through the Users can try Microsoft Fabric paid features tenant setting. Scoping it to specific security groups (for example AnalyticsTeam and FabricAdmins) lets only the PoC team start the trial, instead of the whole organization.

  • Option E: Users can create Fabric items controls who can create Fabric (non Power BI) items. Enabling it only for specific security groups ensures that only the PoC team can create the lakehouses, warehouses, pipelines and notebooks, and nobody else in the tenant can create them before the PoC is finished. Using an allow list is the least-privilege approach.

answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Enable the Users can try Microsoft Fabric paid features option for the entire organization.

Why it is incorrect: Enabling it for everyone would let all Litware users start a Fabric trial, contradicting the requirement that the rest of the users get access to Fabric only after the PoC, and violating least privilege.

C. Enable the Allow Azure Active Directory guest users to access Microsoft Fabric option for specific security groups.

Why it is incorrect: The PoC is an internal exercise for the Litware analytics team; the case does not mention any external or guest users, so granting guest access is unnecessary and goes against least privilege.

D. Enable the Users can create Fabric items option and exclude specific security groups.

Why it is incorrect: Enabling it for the entire organization and excluding groups is a deny-list approach: everybody except the excluded groups could create Fabric items, including users that are outside the PoC team.   • Mode, DirectQuery — Why it is incorrect: DirectQuery sends every query of every visual to the source; it is slower and does not minimize execution time.
  • Mode, Import — Why it is incorrect: Import is fast but only shows new data after a refresh, violating 'as soon as they are updated'.

You need to implement the date dimension in the data store. The solution must meet the technical requirements.

What are two ways to achieve the goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
options: Populate the date dimension table by using a dataflow.
Populate the date dimension table by using a Copy activity in a pipeline.
Populate the date dimension view by using T-SQL.
Populate the date dimension table by using a Stored procedure activity in a pipeline.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Option A: Populate the date dimension table by using a dataflow.
  • Option D: Populate the date dimension table by using a Stored procedure activity in a pipeline.

Why they are correct: crossing the case study's technical requirements with Microsoft Fabric capabilities:

  • No source and dynamic range: “there is no existing data source for the date dimension” and “the date dimension must always contain dates from 2010 through the end of the current year”.
  • Option A (Dataflow Gen2): Power Query M functions (such as List.Dates from #date(2010,1,1) to Date.EndOfYear(DateTime.LocalNow())) can generate the whole calendar table with its fiscal and natural attributes and write it to a physical warehouse table without any external source. It also meets the team's preference for low-code tools.
  • Option D (Stored procedure activity in a pipeline): the warehouse supports T-SQL stored procedures that generate the range from 2010-01-01 to DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(GETDATE()), 12, 31) (using a numbers table or recursion/loops) and insert or update the physical DimDate table. Invoking it from a pipeline automates daily execution before the fact tables are populated.
  • Why it must be a physical table and not a view: the semantic models must include only dimensional-model objects and minimize query execution time. Physical Delta tables let models run in pure Direct Lake mode with no fallback to DirectQuery (which does happen when querying SQL views).
  • Official documentation: Dataflow Gen2 overview in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn | Stored procedure activity in Data Factory for Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn | Create date tables in Power BI Desktop and Fabric - Microsoft Learn
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

  • Option B: Populate the date dimension table by using a Copy activity in a pipeline — Why it is incorrect: The Copy activity moves data from an existing source to a destination. Since the statement says no data source exists for the date dimension, there is nothing to copy the records from. Official documentation: Copy activity in Data Factory for Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn
  • Option C: Populate the date dimension view by using T-SQL — Why it is incorrect: For two reasons: a view is a stored virtual query that is not “populated” with physical data; and using a view for the dimensional model would prevent the semantic model from running in Direct Lake without falling back to DirectQuery, degrading performance versus a physical table and contradicting the requirement to minimize report query execution time. Official documentation: T-SQL surface area in Microsoft Fabric - Microsoft Learn | Direct Lake overview (fallback) - Microsoft Learn

q063.stem:
You need to ensure the data loading activities in the AnalyticsPOC workspace are executed in the appropriate sequence. The solution must meet the technical requirements.

What should you do?
options: Create a dataflow that has multiple steps and schedule the dataflow.
Create and schedule a Spark notebook.
Create and schedule a Spark job definition.
Create a pipeline that has dependencies between activities and schedule the pipeline.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Create a pipeline that has dependencies between activities and schedule the pipeline.

Why it is correct: The technical requirements say the raw and cleansed data must be updated completely before the dimensional model is populated, and the analytics engineers load the AnalyticsPOC store daily using a mix of tools (low-code ingestion, dataflows, notebooks and T-SQL). A Fabric data pipeline is the orchestration item: you chain activities (Copy, Dataflow, Notebook, Stored procedure, and so on) with dependency conditions such as On success, so an activity starts only when the previous one has finished successfully, and you attach a schedule to run the whole chain daily. That guarantees the required order with minimal effort.

  • Official documentation: Activity overview - Microsoft Fabric
  • Official documentation: Concept: Data pipeline runs - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Create a dataflow that has multiple steps and schedule the dataflow.

Why it is incorrect: The steps of a dataflow are Power Query transformation steps inside one dataflow, not an orchestration of the different load processes (ingestion, cleansing, dimensional-model load). A dataflow cannot sequence notebooks, stored procedures or other items, and the case lets engineers pick any transformation tool.

  • Official documentation: Dataflow activity - Microsoft Fabric

B. Create and schedule a Spark notebook.

Why it is incorrect: A scheduled notebook only runs its own code. It is not designed to coordinate the other load items (dataflows, copy jobs, T-SQL procedures) and would require custom orchestration code. A pipeline Notebook activity is the right way to include notebooks in a sequence.

  • Official documentation: Activity overview - Microsoft Fabric

C. Create and schedule a Spark job definition.

Why it is incorrect: A Spark job definition runs a single Spark application. As with a notebook, it cannot orchestrate dependencies between different kinds of load activities, so it does not guarantee the required sequence across the whole process.

  • Official documentation: Job scheduler in Microsoft Fabric

You are implementing a medallion architecture in a single Fabric workspace.

You have a lakehouse that contains the Bronze and Silver layers and a warehouse that contains the Gold layer.

You create the items required to populate the layers as shown in the following table.

You need to ensure that the layers are populated daily in sequential order such that Silver is populated only after Bronze is complete, and Gold is populated only after Silver is complete. The solution must minimize development effort and complexity.

What should you use to execute each set of items? To answer, drag the appropriate options to the correct items. Each option may be used once, more than once, or not at all. You may need to drag the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Orchestration pipeline: A schedule
  • Bronze layer: An Invoke pipeline activity
  • Silver layer: A pipeline Dataflow activity
  • Gold layer: A pipeline Stored procedure activity

Why it is correct: to orchestrate a medallion architecture by running already-created items (child pipelines, dataflows and stored procedures) daily and in strict order, with minimal effort and complexity, you use a master orchestration pipeline with On success dependencies between activities:

  • Orchestration pipeline, A schedule: the layers must be loaded daily: the orchestration pipeline is scheduled to start the whole flow at a fixed time.
  • Bronze layer, An Invoke pipeline activity: the Bronze items are pipelines with Copy activities; Invoke pipeline runs them and waits for them to finish.
  • Silver layer, A pipeline Dataflow activity: Silver is loaded with dataflows; the Dataflow activity runs them after Bronze succeeds.
  • Gold layer, A pipeline Stored procedure activity: Gold is built with stored procedures; the Stored procedure activity runs the T-SQL in the required order.

Incorrect options:

  • Orchestration pipeline, A pipeline Copy activity — Why it is incorrect: it is an activity that runs inside the pipeline, not what triggers it every day.
  • Orchestration pipeline, A pipeline Dataflow activity — Why it is incorrect: it is an activity inside the pipeline, not a schedule.
  • Orchestration pipeline, A pipeline Stored procedure activity — Why it is incorrect: it is an activity inside the pipeline, not a schedule.
  • Orchestration pipeline, A Spark job definition — Why it is incorrect: no layer uses Spark and it is not a schedule.
  • Orchestration pipeline, An Invoke pipeline activity — Why it is incorrect: it is an activity inside the pipeline, not a schedule.
  • Bronze layer, A pipeline Copy activity — Why it is incorrect: Copy pipelines already exist; adding it would duplicate logic instead of reusing it with Invoke pipeline.
  • Bronze layer, A pipeline Dataflow activity — Why it is incorrect: the Bronze items are pipelines, not dataflows.
  • Bronze layer, A pipeline Stored procedure activity — Why it is incorrect: the Bronze items are pipelines, not stored procedures.
  • Bronze layer, A schedule — Why it is incorrect: a schedule starts the flow, but it does not run an item inside the sequence.
  • Bronze layer, A Spark job definition — Why it is incorrect: no layer uses Spark; it would add unnecessary code.
  • Silver layer, A pipeline Copy activity — Why it is incorrect: Copy is already used in Bronze and Silver is loaded with dataflows.
  • Silver layer, A pipeline Stored procedure activity — Why it is incorrect: it is T-SQL for the Gold layer, not Silver.
  • Silver layer, A schedule — Why it is incorrect: a schedule does not run a dataflow inside the sequence.
  • Silver layer, A Spark job definition — Why it is incorrect: no layer uses Spark.
  • Silver layer, An Invoke pipeline activity — Why it is incorrect: it calls pipelines, not dataflows.
  • Gold layer, A pipeline Copy activity — Why it is incorrect: Gold is built with T-SQL in the warehouse, not with copies.
  • Gold layer, A pipeline Dataflow activity — Why it is incorrect: Gold does not use dataflows in this design.
  • Gold layer, A schedule — Why it is incorrect: a schedule does not run stored procedures inside the sequence.
  • Gold layer, A Spark job definition — Why it is incorrect: no layer uses Spark.
  • Gold layer, An Invoke pipeline activity — Why it is incorrect: it calls pipelines; it does not run T-SQL directly.
