q189.stem:
You have a Fabric warehouse that contains a table named Table1. Table1 contains three columns named SalesAmount, ProductCategory, and

TransactionDate.

You need to create a Microsoft Power BI query that will calculate the total sales amount of each product category for transactions that occurred during the last quarter.

Which two actions should you perform in the visual query editor? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
options: For the TransactionDate column, select Remove duplicates.
For the TransactionDate column, select Keep top rows and set Number of rows to 90.
For the TransactionDate column, select Filter rows and set the value to last quarter.
For the ProductCategory column, select Group by and sum the SalesAmount column.
For the SalesAmount column, select Transformation number column - Standard, select Add, and then set the value to 90.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: For the TransactionDate column, select Filter rows and set the value to last quarter.
  • Option D: For the ProductCategory column, select Group by and sum the SalesAmount column.

Why it is correct: the Fabric warehouse visual query editor offers a no-code, Power Query-based interface that translates transformations into T-SQL queries. To meet both requirements of the question:

Filter by the last quarter (option C): using Filter rows on TransactionDate with the relative date filter last quarter, the editor generates the WHERE clause that limits transactions to the previous quarter.

Group by category and sum sales (option D): using Group by on ProductCategory with the Sum aggregation on SalesAmount, the editor generates the GROUP BY and SUM(SalesAmount) clauses that give the total sales amount per category.

  • Option A, Remove duplicates on TransactionDate: it would discard valid transactions from the same date (one row per day), distorting the total, and it does not filter by the last quarter.
  • Option B, Keep top rows with 90 rows: it keeps only the first 90 rows of the table (equivalent to SELECT TOP 90), unrelated to a date range or the last quarter.
  • Option E, Add 90 on SalesAmount: it adds 90 to the amount of each transaction; it neither filters dates nor totals sales by category.
  • Official documentation: Query using the visual query editor, Query a warehouse in Microsoft Fabric

links.t: Query using the visual query editor
Query a warehouse in Microsoft Fabric

q190.stem:
You have a Microsoft Power BI semantic model.

You need to identify any surrogate key columns in the model that have the Summarize By property set to a value other than to None. The solution must minimize effort.

What should you use?
options: Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop
Model explorer in Microsoft Power BI Desktop
Model view in Microsoft Power BI Desktop

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Model view in Microsoft Power BI Desktop

Why it is correct: In Model view, you can select several columns, or all columns of several tables, and the Properties pane applies the changes to every selected field, so you can see and fix the Summarize by property (and others such as Hidden) in bulk. This lets you scan the surrogate key columns, spot the ones whose Summarize by is not None, and set them to None in a few clicks, which is the lowest-effort approach compared with opening each column in Data view.

  • Official documentation: Work with Model view in Power BI Desktop
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop

Why it is incorrect: Performance Analyzer records how long each report visual takes to load and which DAX queries it runs. It does not show or edit column properties such as Summarize by.

  • Official documentation: Work with Model view in Power BI Desktop

B. Model explorer in Microsoft Power BI Desktop

Why it is incorrect: Model explorer is a tree view of the model objects (tables, columns, measures, relationships) with the number of items in each node. It helps you navigate the model but is not where you review and bulk-edit the Summarize by value across columns, which is done in the Properties pane of Model view.

  • Official documentation: Work with Model view in Power BI Desktop

D. DAX Formatter in DAX Studio

Why it is incorrect: DAX Formatter only reformats DAX expressions for readability. It has no view of column properties like Summarize by.

  • Official documentation: Work with Model view in Power BI Desktop

q191.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a warehouse.

You use a dataflow to load a new dataset from OneLake to the warehouse.

You need to add a Power Query step to identify the maximum values for the numeric columns.

Which function should you include in the step?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Table.Profile

Why it is correct: The requirement is to add a Power Query step in the dataflow that identifies the maximum values for the numeric columns of the new dataset. Table.Profile is the Power Query M function designed for exactly this: it returns a table with one row per column of the input table, and for each column it calculates profile statistics where they apply, namely minimum, maximum, average, standard deviation, count, null count and distinct count. A single step therefore gives you the maximum of every numeric column at once, which is what the "column profiling" feature of the Power Query editor is built on. The result can then be inspected or filtered before the data is loaded into the warehouse.

  • Official documentation: Table.Profile - Power Query M
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Table.Range

Why it is incorrect: Table.Range returns a subset of rows of a table, starting at a given offset and for a given number of rows. It is a row-slicing function by position; it does not calculate any statistics and does not look at the values of the numeric columns, so it cannot identify their maximum values.

  • Official documentation: Table.Range - Power Query M

B. Table.MaxN

Why it is incorrect: Table.MaxN returns the N rows of a table that have the largest values for one column (or comparison criteria) that you specify. It returns rows, not a per-column maximum, and it works on a single criterion at a time. To get the maximum of every numeric column you would need to repeat it for each column and still extract the value; the profile function gives all of them in a single step.

  • Official documentation: Table.MaxN - Power Query M

links.t: Table.Profile - Power Query M
Table.Range - Power Query M
Table.MaxN - Power Query M

q192.stem:
-

You have a Fabric warehouse named Warehouse1 that contains a table named TaxiTrips.

TaxiTrips contains the following columns.

You need to create a query that shows the top three taxi companies based on the total miles traveled.

How should you complete the T-SQL statement? To answer, select the

appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • SELECT ...: Top (3)
  • Second box (after FROM): GROUP BY company
  • Third box (before DESC): ORDER BY sum(tripDistance)

Why it is correct: The completed statement is SELECT TOP (3) company AS TaxiCompany, sum(passengerCount) AS TotalPassengers, sum(tripDistance) TotalDistance FROM [Warehouse1].[dbo].[TaxiTrips] GROUP BY company ORDER BY sum(tripDistance) DESC;

  • SELECT ..., Top (3): in T-SQL the number of rows is limited with TOP (n) right after SELECT; with ORDER BY … DESC it returns the three companies with the most miles.
  • Second box (after FROM), GROUP BY company: with aggregates, every non-aggregated SELECT column must be in GROUP BY, and you group by the real column name: company.
  • Third box (before DESC), ORDER BY sum(tripDistance): you sort by the total miles per company, so the expression is the aggregate: ORDER BY sum(tripDistance).

Incorrect options:

  • SELECT ..., FETCH NEXT 3 ROWS ONLY — Why it is incorrect: FETCH NEXT 3 ROWS ONLY is valid T-SQL, but it is part of ORDER BY … OFFSET and does not go right after SELECT.
  • SELECT ..., Limit (3) — Why it is incorrect: Limit (3) is not T-SQL (it is MySQL, PostgreSQL, Spark SQL).
  • Second box (after FROM), GROUP BY TaxiCompany — Why it is incorrect: GROUP BY TaxiCompany uses an alias; GROUP BY is evaluated before SELECT and the alias is not visible.
  • Second box (after FROM), ORDER BY tripDistance — Why it is incorrect: ORDER BY tripDistance does not group; company would remain ungrouped and raise an error.
  • Third box (before DESC), GROUP BY company — Why it is incorrect: GROUP BY company was already used and cannot be repeated before DESC.
  • Third box (before DESC), ORDER BY tripDistance — Why it is incorrect: ORDER BY tripDistance sorts by a non-aggregated, non-grouped column: invalid in a grouped query and it does not represent the total.
  • Official documentation: TOP (Transact-SQL), SELECT - ORDER BY clause (Transact-SQL), SELECT (Transact-SQL)

q193.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains the workspaces shown in the following table.

You have a deployment pipeline named Pipeline1 that deploys items from Workspace_DEV to Workspace_TEST. In Pipeline1, all items that have matching names are paired.

You deploy the contents of Workspace_DEV to Workspace_TEST by using

Pipeline1.

What will the contents of Workspace_TEST be once the deployment is complete?
options: Lakehouse1 - Lakehouse2 - Notebook1 - Notebook2 - Pipeline1 - SemanticModel1 -

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Lakehouse1, Lakehouse2, Notebook1, Notebook2, Pipeline1, SemanticModel1

Why it is correct: A deployment pipeline only overwrites an item in the target stage when that item is paired with the source item. Items that exist in the source but are not paired in the target are copied as new items, and items that exist only in the target are left untouched. Applying this to the scenario:

  • Lakehouse1, Notebook1 and Pipeline1 exist in Workspace_DEV but have no paired counterpart in Workspace_TEST, so they are created as new items in Workspace_TEST.
  • SemanticModel1 has the same name in both workspaces and, according to the question, items with matching names are paired, so the one in Workspace_TEST is overwritten with the DEV version (it remains a single item).
  • Lakehouse2 and Notebook2 exist only in Workspace_TEST. They have no source counterpart, so the deployment does not delete or change them.

The final content of Workspace_TEST is therefore the union of both: Lakehouse1, Lakehouse2, Notebook1, Notebook2, Pipeline1 and SemanticModel1.

  • Official documentation: Get started with deployment pipelines - Microsoft Fabric and Assign a workspace to a deployment pipeline (item pairing)
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Lakehouse2, Notebook2, SemanticModel1

Why it is incorrect: This would mean that the new items from DEV (Lakehouse1, Notebook1, Pipeline1) were not deployed. A deployment copies every supported item that does not yet exist in the target stage; only items that are already paired are overwritten rather than duplicated.

  • Official documentation: Get started with deployment pipelines - Microsoft Fabric

B. Lakehouse1, Notebook1, Pipeline1, SemanticModel1

Why it is incorrect: This answer assumes that the deployment replaces the whole content of the target workspace so that it becomes a mirror of DEV, removing Lakehouse2 and Notebook2. Deployment pipelines do not delete items from the target stage that have no counterpart in the source stage; those items "remain as is".

  • Official documentation: Get started with deployment pipelines - Microsoft Fabric

D. Lakehouse2, Notebook2, Pipeline1, SemanticModel1

Why it is incorrect: It includes Pipeline1 and SemanticModel1 but omits Lakehouse1 and Notebook1, which exist in DEV, are not paired in TEST and are therefore deployed as new items. Nothing in the scenario excludes lakehouses or notebooks from the deployment.

  • Official documentation: Assign a workspace to a deployment pipeline (item pairing)

q194.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a workspace named Workspace1 and a user named User1. Workspace1 contains a warehouse named DW1.

You share DW1 with User1 and assign User1 the default permissions for DW1.

What can User1 do?
options: Read data from the tables in DW1.
Build reports by using the default dataset.
Read the underlying Parquet files from OneLake.
Connect to DW1 via the TDS (Tabular Data Stream) endpoint.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Connect to DW1 via the TDS (Tabular Data Stream) endpoint.

Why it is correct: When you share a warehouse and do not select any additional permission, the recipient receives only the Read permission on the item. This permission allows the user to connect to the warehouse's SQL endpoint (the TDS endpoint), which is the equivalent of CONNECT in SQL Server. It does not allow the user to query any table or view, execute functions or procedures, or read the files in OneLake, unless more access is explicitly granted afterwards through the additional sharing options (for example "Read all data using SQL") or by using T-SQL GRANT statements on specific objects.

  • Official documentation: Share your warehouse and manage permissions - Microsoft Fabric
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Read data from the tables in DW1.

Why it is incorrect: Reading table data requires the additional ReadData permission ("Read all data using SQL") or granular T-SQL permissions such as GRANT SELECT. With only the default Read permission, the user can connect but cannot query any table or view.

  • Official documentation: Share your warehouse and manage permissions - Microsoft Fabric

B. Build reports by using the default dataset.

Why it is incorrect: Building reports requires Build permission on the semantic model, and reports in Direct Lake or DirectQuery mode over the warehouse also need data access (ReadData or granular permissions). The default Read permission grants none of these, so the user cannot build reports from the default semantic model.

  • Official documentation: Share your warehouse and manage permissions - Microsoft Fabric

C. Read the underlying Parquet files from OneLake.

Why it is incorrect: Access to the warehouse's underlying files in OneLake requires the ReadAll permission ("Read all data using Apache Spark"), which is only granted when you select it explicitly while sharing. It is not part of the default permissions.

  • Official documentation: Share your warehouse and manage permissions - Microsoft Fabric

q195.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains two workspaces named Workspace1 and Workspace2.

Workspace1 is used as the development environment. Workspace2 is used as the production environment. Each environment uses a different storage account.

Workspace1 contains a Dataflow Gen2 named Dataflow1. The data source of Dataflow1 is a CSV file in blob storage.

You plan to implement a deployment pipeline to deploy items from Workspace1 to Workspace2.

You need to ensure that the data source references the correct location in the production environment.

What should you do?
options: Create a data source rule only.
Create a data source rule and a parameter rule.
After implementing the deployment pipeline, manually change the data source

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Create a data source rule and a parameter rule.

Why it is correct: The key requirement is that, after the deployment from Workspace1 (development) to Workspace2 (production), the dataflow reads its CSV file from the production storage account instead of the development one. In a deployment pipeline, the configuration that differs between stages is handled with deployment rules, so that no manual change is needed after every deployment. The source is a CSV file in blob storage, so the connection information appears in two places: the data source (the storage account) and the parameters that point to the file location or path. Setting a data source rule for the storage account and a parameter rule for the file location makes sure that both parts reference the production environment once the content is deployed.

⚠️ Heads-up: The study source marks this answer, but the current Microsoft Learn documentation on deployment rules lists them for Dataflow Gen1, semantic models, paginated reports, mirrored databases and notebooks, and the Dataflow Gen2 CI/CD architecture article states that deployment rules do not alter Dataflow Gen2 connections or mashup logic (parameters or variable libraries are recommended instead). Option C is still the best of the choices offered, since changing the source manually after deployment is an anti-pattern. Check it against the linked documentation.

  • Official documentation: Create deployment rules - Microsoft Fabric and Dataflow Gen2 CI/CD and ALM solution architecture
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. Create a data source rule only.

Why it is incorrect: A data source rule only swaps the data source connection (for example the storage account) for another one of the same type. The location of the CSV file inside the source (container, folder or file name) is usually held in a parameter, which would still point to the development value after the deployment, so a data source rule alone does not fully fix the reference.

  • Official documentation: Create deployment rules - Microsoft Fabric

B. Create a parameter rule only.

Why it is incorrect: A parameter rule changes the value of a parameter, but the question states that each environment uses a different storage account, which is a data source connection change. Without the data source rule, the connection would keep pointing to the development storage account.

  • Official documentation: Create deployment rules - Microsoft Fabric

D. After implementing the deployment pipeline, manually change the data source

Why it is incorrect: A manual change after every deployment is error-prone and defeats the purpose of deployment pipelines, which provide deployment rules precisely to automate environment-specific settings. Moreover, the next deployment would overwrite the manual change with the development configuration.

  • Official documentation: Create deployment rules - Microsoft Fabric

q196.stem:
You have a semantic model named Model1 that contains data that relates to customers and their bank account balances.

Model1 has the following tables and columns.

A customer can have one or more accounts. Each account can be associated to multiple customers.

You need to ensure that users can query Model1 to identify the total transaction amounts by customer.

What should you add to Model1?
options: a many-to-many relationship between FactTransaction and Dim Customer
a bridge table with relationships to DimCustomer and DimAccount
a bridge table with relationships to FactTransaction and DimCustomer
the CustomerKey column in FactTransaction and a relationship to DimCustomer

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: a bridge table with relationships to DimCustomer and DimAccount

Why it is correct: The statement says that a customer can have several accounts and an account can be associated with several customers: this is a many-to-many relationship between DimCustomer and DimAccount. FactTransaction holds the transaction amounts and already relates to DimAccount through AccountKey, so the missing link is between customers and accounts. The recommended modeling pattern is to add a bridge table (a factless table with one row per customer-account association) that has a one-to-many relationship from DimCustomer to the bridge and another one-to-many relationship from DimAccount to the bridge. The filter then flows DimCustomer -> bridge -> DimAccount -> FactTransaction (the relationship between DimAccount and the bridge must propagate the filter toward the account, typically configured as bidirectional), so you can sum Amount by customer. Microsoft's guidance specifically recommends this approach and advises against relating the two dimensions directly with a many-to-many cardinality.

  • Official documentation: Many-to-many relationship guidance - Power BI
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. a many-to-many relationship between FactTransaction and Dim Customer

Why it is incorrect: FactTransaction has no customer column; its link to the dimensions is the AccountKey. A direct many-to-many relationship would need a common column between the two tables, and the guidance recommends not relating fact and dimension tables through many-to-many cardinality when a bridge table can resolve the association properly.

  • Official documentation: Many-to-many relationships in Power BI Desktop

C. a bridge table with relationships to FactTransaction and DimCustomer

Why it is incorrect: The bridge table must resolve the many-to-many association between customers and accounts, so it must connect DimCustomer and DimAccount. FactTransaction should keep its relationship with DimAccount through AccountKey; connecting the bridge directly to the fact table would leave the account dimension out of the path and bypass the proper star schema design.

  • Official documentation: Many-to-many relationship guidance - Power BI

D. the CustomerKey column in FactTransaction and a relationship to DimCustomer

Why it is incorrect: Adding CustomerKey to the fact table would assign each transaction to a single customer, but an account can belong to several customers, so a transaction cannot be attributed to just one of them. It would also require changing the fact grain and the source data, and it does not model the actual many-to-many association.

  • Official documentation: Many-to-many relationship guidance - Power BI

q197.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains 30 CSV files in OneLake. The files are updated daily.

You create a Microsoft Power BI semantic model named Model1 that uses the CSV files as a data source. You configure incremental refresh for Model1 and publish the model to an F64 capacity in the Fabric tenant.

When you initiate a refresh of Model1, the refresh fails after running out of resources.

What is a possible cause of the failure?
options: XMLA Endpoint is set to Read Only.
The data type of the column used to partition the data has changed.
Only refresh complete days is selected.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option E: Query folding is NOT occurring.

Why it is correct: Incremental refresh relies on the RangeStart and RangeEnd parameters filtering the source so that only the rows of the partitions being refreshed are requested. When the data source supports query folding, that filter is pushed down to the source. When folding does not occur, the Power Query mashup engine has to retrieve all the rows of the table from the source and apply the filter locally, which can make the refresh slow and cause it to run out of resources, "effectively defeating the purpose of incremental refresh". CSV files are a source that does not support query folding, so a refresh that fails after running out of resources is consistent with the filter being applied after loading all 30 files. Folding is also the thing to verify before enabling incremental refresh.

  • Official documentation: Configure incremental refresh and real-time data for Power BI semantic models and Power Query query folding guidance
answer.incorrect:
Incorrect options:

A. XMLA Endpoint is set to Read Only.

Why it is incorrect: The XMLA endpoint setting controls whether external tools can read or write to the model's metadata and data (for example, deploying changes or running TMSL refresh commands). Scheduled or manual refreshes initiated from the Fabric service are not blocked by this setting, and it has no relation to running out of resources.

  • Official documentation: Configure incremental refresh and real-time data for Power BI semantic models

B. Query folding is occurring.

Why it is incorrect: Query folding is the desired behavior: the date filter is evaluated at the source and only the necessary rows are retrieved, which reduces memory and time. It would help avoid, not cause, a resource failure.

  • Official documentation: Power Query query folding guidance

C. The data type of the column used to partition the data has changed.

Why it is incorrect: The column used for the incremental refresh policy must be of the Date/Time type to match RangeStart and RangeEnd. A change in the data type produces a specific error in the incremental refresh configuration or a schema mismatch when refreshing, not a failure due to running out of resources.

  • Official documentation: Troubleshoot incremental refresh and real-time data

D. Only refresh complete days is selected.

Why it is incorrect: This option only ensures that the refresh period covers entire days, so rows that arrive during the day are not partially loaded. It affects which period is refreshed, not the volume of data retrieved from the source or the use of resources.

  • Official documentation: Configure incremental refresh and real-time data for Power BI semantic models

You are implementing two dimension tables named Customers and Products in a Fabric warehouse.

You need to create two slowly changing dimensions that meet the requirements shown in the following table.

Which type of SCD should you use for each table? To answer, drag the appropriate SCD types to the correct tables. Each SCD type may be used once, more than once, or not at all. You may need to drag the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Customers: Type 2
  • Products: Type 1

Why it is correct: Analysis of each selection:

  • Customers, Type 2: SCD Type 2 inserts a new row (new surrogate key and validity dates) on each change: it keeps the full history.
  • Products, Type 1: SCD Type 1 overwrites the attribute in the current record without keeping history.

Incorrect options:

  • Customers, Type 0 — Why it is incorrect: Type 0 never changes attribute values.
  • Customers, Type 1 — Why it is incorrect: Type 1 erases history instead of keeping versions.
  • Customers, Type 3 — Why it is incorrect: Type 3 only keeps limited history (previous value in an extra column).
  • Products, Type 0 — Why it is incorrect: Type 0 means the value is never updated.
  • Products, Type 2 — Why it is incorrect: Type 2 would create new rows and keep history, which the requirement does not want.
  • Products, Type 3 — Why it is incorrect: Type 3 stores the previous value in an extra column instead of simply overwriting.
  • Official documentation: Implement slowly changing dimensions - Design dimensional models in Fabric, Slowly changing dimension type 2 - Microsoft Fabric, Slowly changing dimension type 1 - Microsoft Fabric, Dimensional modeling: dimension tables - Fabric warehouse

You have a Fabric eventhouse that contains a KQL database. The database contains a table named TaxiData that stores the following data.

You need to create a column named FirstPickupDateTime that will contain the first value of each hour from tpep_pickup_datetime partitioned by

payment_type.

How should you complete the query? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answers:

  • Function: Row_window_session
  • Comparison operator: !=

Why it is correct: The completed query is TaxiData | sort by tpep_pickup_datetime asc, payment_type asc | extend FirstPickupDateTime = row_window_session(tpep_pickup_datetime, 1h, 0m, payment_type != prev(payment_type)).

  • Function, Row_window_session: row_window_session returns the first value of each row's session in a serialized table: here, the first value of each hour.
  • Comparison operator, !=: Restart evaluates to true when the payment type differs from the previous row: payment_type != prev(payment_type).

Incorrect options:

  • Function, Row_cumsum — Why it is incorrect: row_cumsum computes a numeric running sum, not the first datetime of a window.
  • Function, Row_rank_dense — Why it is incorrect: row_rank_dense returns a numeric rank, not the first value of the session.
  • Function, Row_rank_min — Why it is incorrect: row_rank_min returns a numeric rank, not the first value of the session.
  • Comparison operator, <= — Why it is incorrect: <= would depend on value order and would not restart reliably at group boundaries.
  • Comparison operator, == — Why it is incorrect: == would restart the session on every row repeating the same payment type, the opposite of the intent.
  • Comparison operator, >= — Why it is incorrect: >= would depend on value order and would not restart reliably at group boundaries.
  • Official documentation: row_window_session() - Kusto Query Language, Window functions overview

q200.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains four workspaces named Development, Test, QA, and Production. All the workspaces are in Premium Per User (PPU) license mode.

You plan to use a release pipeline to support the development lifecycle from Development to Production.

Which three actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Step 1: Create a deployment pipeline.
  • Step 2: Create the QA stage.
  • Step 3: Assign workspaces.

Why it is correct: the four workspaces are already on PPU, which meets the capacity requirements; the sequence for a four-stage pipeline is:

  • Step 1, Create a deployment pipeline.: first you create the deployment pipeline from the deployment pipelines menu.
  • Step 2, Create the QA stage.: Fabric defines three stages by default; for four environments you add and name the QA stage before finishing creation (number and names are permanent).
  • Step 3, Assign workspaces.: with the structure created, each workspace is assigned to its stage to enable content promotion.

Incorrect options:

  • Move each workspace to Pro license mode — Why it is incorrect: pipelines require Fabric (F), Premium (P) or PPU capacity; Pro mode does not support them.
  • Create a deployment rule — Why it is incorrect: rules are optional and are defined after assigning workspaces and having deployed items; they are not part of the initial steps.
  • Official documentation: Get started with deployment pipelines, Understand the deployment process, Fabric lifecycle management tools: FAQ, Create deployment rules

q201.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1 and a user named User1.

You need to ensure that User1 can read all the data in Lakehouse1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
options: Assign the Contributor role to User1.
Assign the Viewer role to User1.
Share Lakehouse1 by using item permissions.
Assign the Member role to User1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Select Read all Apache Spark.
  • Option D: Share Lakehouse1 by using item permissions.

Why it is correct: Workspace roles give access to all the items in the workspace, which goes beyond least privilege. The right approach is to share only Lakehouse1 with User1 (item permissions) and, in the sharing dialog, select Read all Apache Spark, which lets the user read all the OneLake files and tables of the lakehouse.

  • Option A, Contributor: it is a workspace role: it gives access to every item and also allows writing; it exceeds least privilege.
  • Option C, Viewer: it is a workspace role: it gives access to every item in the workspace, not only Lakehouse1.
  • Option E, Member: it is a workspace role: it gives access to every item and allows writing and sharing; it exceeds least privilege.

q202.stem:
You have a Microsoft Power BI semantic model that contains a single table named Orders. Orders contains the following columns: Product Name, Order Date and Quantity.

You have a Power BI report that contains a page named Inventory. Inventory contains a slicer for the Product Name column and a clustered column chart that shows Quantity by Order Date.

You need to ensure that users can select whether to display Quantity by Product Name or Quantity by Order Date in the chart. The solution must minimize development effort.

What should you create?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: a field parameter.

Why it is correct: A field parameter lets users pick, with a slicer, which fields or measures a visual shows (here, the chart axis: Product Name or Order Date) without hand-writing DAX; it is created in Power BI Desktop with a single menu option.

  • Option A, a measure: it returns a calculated value, but it does not let the user change which field appears on the chart axis.
  • Option B, a dynamic format string: it only changes how a measure is displayed (currency, decimals…); it does not swap the fields on the axis.
  • Option D, a calculation group: it modifies calculations over measures (for example, time intelligence), not the field used on the axis, and takes more effort (Tabular Editor) than a field parameter.
  • Official documentation: Use field parameters in Power BI

links.t: Use field parameters in Power BI

q203.stem:
You have three Fabric workspaces named Workspace1, Workspace2 and Workspace3. Workspace1 contains a report named Report1 and a semantic model named Model1 in Import mode.

You perform these actions: create a deployment pipeline named Pipeline1 with three stages (development, test and production); assign Workspace1 to development, Workspace2 to test and Workspace3 to production; and modify Model1.

You need to ensure that changes to Model1 are available in the production stage as quickly as possible. The solution must NOT affect the availability of Report1.

Which three actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Step 1: Run Pipeline1 from the development stage to the test stage.
  • Step 2: Run Pipeline1 from the test stage to the production stage.
  • Step 3: Refresh Model1 in the production stage.

Why it is correct: deployment pipelines copy only metadata and definitions, not the model's data; to get the changes to production as soon as possible the sequence is:

  • Step 1, Run Pipeline1 from the development stage to the test stage.: promotion is sequential between adjacent stages: first Model1's metadata is deployed from development to test (selective deployment).
  • Step 2, Run Pipeline1 from the test stage to the production stage.: promotion does not require loaded data in the test stage, so it is promoted straight from test to production.
  • Step 3, Refresh Model1 in the production stage.: the Import model has no data in production until refreshed there; refreshing it loads data with the new structure and avoids errors in Report1.

Incorrect options:

  • Refresh Model1 in the development stage — Why it is incorrect: it only reloads the development cache; pipelines never transfer data, so it adds nothing to production.
  • Refresh Model1 in the test stage — Why it is incorrect: it is not required to promote metadata nor does it transfer data to production, and it would delay delivery.
  • Official documentation: Understand the deployment process, Get started with deployment pipelines

Get started with deployment pipelines

q204.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a semantic model named Model1. Model1 contains the following tables.

Product and Store can be part of multiple campaigns, and multiple active campaigns can exist simultaneously.

You plan to create a report named Report1 that will display sales made after a campaign for a given store.

You need to add a table to Model1 and configure cardinality for the table's relationships. What should you configure?

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Type of table: Bridging
  • Cardinality: One-to-many

Why it is correct: In Model1, Product (with ProductID) and Store (with StoreID) can take part in several campaigns at the same time; the Campaign table holds the campaign attributes (CampaignDate, CampaignID, Name, Description) together with ProductID and StoreID, and the Sales table records only SalesDate, StoreID and ProductID. This is the classic many-to-many scenario, where Power BI also does not allow direct relationships based on a two-column composite key (StoreID + ProductID) between Campaign and Sales.

  • Type of table, Bridging: a bridge table stores the unique key combinations and propagates filters deterministically to Sales in a many-to-many relationship.
  • Cardinality, One-to-many: the purpose of the bridge table is to avoid direct many-to-many relationships: dimensions connect to it with one-to-many relationships.

Incorrect options:

  • Type of table, Dimension — Why it is incorrect: a standard dimension does not resolve the many-to-many relationship or the composite-key link without filter-path ambiguity.
  • Type of table, Fact — Why it is incorrect: a fact table records events and metrics (like Sales); another one does not create the bridge that propagates filters.
  • Cardinality, Many-to-many — Why it is incorrect: many-to-many would keep duplicates at both ends, degrading performance and creating DAX ambiguity; the bridge breaks it down.
  • Cardinality, One-to-one — Why it is incorrect: one-to-one requires unique keys in both tables; in the bridge the same product or store appears several times.
  • Official documentation: Many-to-many relationship guidance, Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI, Many-to-many relationships in Power BI Desktop, One-to-one relationship guidance

q205.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1.

You have a GitHub repository named Repo1.

You need to connect Workspace1 to the main branch of Repo1.

Which information should you provide?
options: a shared access signature (SAS) token and the branch name of Repo1
a personal access token (PAT) and the URL of Repo1
an access key and the branch name of Repo1
an access key and the URL of Repo1

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: a personal access token (PAT) and the URL of Repo1.

Why it is correct: To connect a workspace to GitHub with Fabric Git integration you add a GitHub account with a personal access token (PAT) and provide the repository URL; you then pick the branch (main) and the folder.

  • Option A, SAS token and branch name: a SAS token is an Azure Storage mechanism, not a GitHub one, and the branch name does not identify the repository.
  • Option C, access key and branch name: access keys belong to Azure Storage and do not authenticate to GitHub; the branch is chosen after connecting with the URL.
  • Option D, access key and URL: the URL is right, but an access key is not a GitHub credential; a personal access token (PAT) is required.

q206.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a semantic model named Model1 that contains the following tables.

You are designing a Microsoft Power BI report named Report1 that will deliver near-real-time (NRT) shipping data about many shipped packages.

You need to ensure that each table is in the appropriate storage mode to support Report1. The solution must support near-real-time data delivery while maintaining high query performance.

Which storage mode should you select for each table? Each mode may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • FactPackageEvents: DirectQuery
  • DimPackage: DirectQuery
  • DimCarrier: Dual

Why it is correct: the model must deliver near real-time data and avoid limited relationships, combining DirectQuery for the large tables and Dual for the small dimension.

  • FactPackageEvents, DirectQuery: it is the events fact table: every query must read the latest events straight from the source, with no scheduled refresh.
  • DimPackage, DirectQuery: it is a large, high-cardinality dimension that grows with the facts; in DirectQuery it shares the source with the fact table and the join is resolved at the source.
  • DimCarrier, Dual: it is a small dimension: in Dual it answers from cache when queried alone and acts as DirectQuery when filtering the fact table, avoiding limited relationships.

Incorrect options:

  • FactPackageEvents, Dual — Why it is incorrect: Dual keeps an in-memory copy that is only updated on refresh: it does not guarantee near real time.
  • FactPackageEvents, Hybrid — Why it is incorrect: Hybrid requires incremental refresh and a date/time column; FactPackageEvents only has PackageID and CarrierID.
  • FactPackageEvents, Import — Why it is incorrect: Import leaves data cached and dependent on refreshes, violating real time.
  • DimPackage, Dual — Why it is incorrect: Dual overloads memory with a large dimension and can become stale.
  • DimPackage, Hybrid — Why it is incorrect: Hybrid is not configured on dimensions and requires date partitioning.
  • DimPackage, Import — Why it is incorrect: Import would consume a lot of memory, require refreshes and could become stale.
  • DimCarrier, DirectQuery — Why it is incorrect: DirectQuery would send to the source queries a small dimension can answer from cache.
  • DimCarrier, Hybrid — Why it is incorrect: Hybrid does not apply to small dimensions without date partitioning.
  • DimCarrier, Import — Why it is incorrect: Import creates limited relationships with the DirectQuery table.
  • Official documentation: Storage mode in Power BI Desktop, Composite model guidance in Power BI, Use composite models in Power BI Desktop, Incremental refresh and real-time data for semantic models

links.t: Storage mode in Power BI Desktop
Composite model guidance in Power BI
Use composite models in Power BI Desktop
Incremental refresh and real-time data for semantic models

q207.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a semantic model named Model1. Model1 contains a fact table with millions of rows of shipment data.

You need to enable partitioning to improve the query performance and manageability of Model1.

Which two tools can you use to achieve the goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Tabular Editor.
  • Option E: Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS).

Why it is correct: Custom partitions of a semantic model are created and managed through the XMLA endpoint with tools that support it: Tabular Editor and SSMS (which also lets you process individual partitions).

  • Option B, DAX Studio: it is used to write DAX queries and analyze model performance, not to create or manage partitions.
  • Option C, Power BI Desktop: it provides no interface to define custom partitions for the published semantic model.
  • Option D, the Power BI service: it lets you configure refresh, but not create custom partitions from its interface; that requires the XMLA endpoint with external tools.
  • Official documentation: Semantic model connectivity with the XMLA endpoint

links.t: Semantic model connectivity with the XMLA endpoint

q208.stem:
You have a Fabric semantic model named Model1 that contains a table named Sales.

You need to enable incremental refresh for the Sales table.

What should you do first?
options: Move Model1 to Premium Per User (PPU) workspace.
From Settings, set Large semantic model storage format to On.
Automate the data preparation by using Dataflow Gen2.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Create parameters in Power Query.

Why it is correct: The first step to set up incremental refresh is to create the RangeStart and RangeEnd date/time parameters in Power Query and use them to filter the table; the incremental refresh policy is defined afterwards.

  • Option A, move to PPU: PPU is not a prerequisite for defining incremental refresh, which also works on other capacities.
  • Option C, large semantic model storage format: it helps with very large models, but it is neither the first step nor a requirement to configure incremental refresh.
  • Option D, Dataflow Gen2: it automates data preparation, but it does not replace the RangeStart/RangeEnd parameters that the policy requires.
  • Official documentation: Configure incremental refresh

links.t: Configure incremental refresh

q209.stem:
You have an Azure SQL database named DB1 and a Fabric workspace named Workspace1. Workspace1 contains a lakehouse named LH1 and a Dataflow Gen2 named Dataflow1. Dataflow1 includes a query named Query1 that loads data from DB1, applies transformations to the data, and then filters the data.

You discover that Query1 loads all the data before applying the transformations.

You need to ensure that Query1 uses query folding. What should you do?
options: Replace DB1 with a Microsoft SQL Server database.
Move the filter steps before the transformation steps in Query1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Move the filter steps before the transformation steps in Query1.

Why it is correct: Query folding translates Power Query steps into a single query at the source, but it breaks as soon as a step the source cannot translate appears. Putting the filter steps before the transformations that prevent folding sends the filter to the source so only the needed data is loaded.

  • Option A, remove unused columns: it reduces data volume, but it does not restore query folding.
  • Option B, incremental refresh: it reduces what is refreshed, but it does not fix the step order that breaks folding.
  • Option C, replace DB1 with SQL Server: DB1 already supports folding; the cause is the step order, not the source.
  • Official documentation: Query folding basics

links.t: Query folding basics

q210.stem:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com and an external user named user1@fabrikam.com.

You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a semantic model named Model1 and a report named Report1. user1@fabrikam.com has access to Report1.

You enable read-write on the XML for Analysis (XMLA) endpoint to provide advanced semantic modeling by using DAX Studio.

You need to provide user1@fabrikam.com with a URL that will enable connectivity by using DAX Studio. How should you complete the URL?

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • First segment: contoso.com
  • Second segment: Workspace1

Why it is correct: The XMLA connection string of a workspace has the format powerbi://api.powerbi.com/v1.0/<tenant>/<workspace>. For a guest (B2B) user the tenant segment is the domain of the tenant that hosts the workspace (contoso.com), not that of their own email, and the second segment is the workspace name (Workspace1); the model is chosen afterwards as the initial catalog in DAX Studio.

  • First segment, contoso.com: for a guest (B2B) user the tenant segment is the domain of the tenant hosting the workspace: contoso.com.
  • Second segment, Workspace1: the second segment is the workspace name: Workspace1; the model is chosen afterwards as the initial catalog in DAX Studio.

Incorrect options:

  • First segment, common — Why it is incorrect: it is a multi-tenant authentication endpoint, not a valid segment of the workspace URL.
  • First segment, fabrikam.com — Why it is incorrect: it is the guest user's domain, not that of the tenant hosting the workspace.
  • First segment, myorg — Why it is incorrect: it only works inside the user's own tenant; an external guest must specify the tenant domain.
  • Second segment, Model1 — Why it is incorrect: the model is not part of the URL; it is chosen as the initial catalog in DAX Studio.
  • Second segment, Report1 — Why it is incorrect: reports are not exposed through the XMLA endpoint; the URL identifies the workspace.
  • Official documentation: Semantic model connectivity with the XMLA endpoint

links.t: Semantic model connectivity with the XMLA endpoint

q211.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 and a warehouse named Warehouse1. Workspace1 contains a user named User1. User1 is assigned the Viewer role for Workspace1.

You need to ensure that User1 can share Warehouse1 with other users. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

Which role should you assign to User1?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Member for Workspace1.

Why it is correct: Sharing items with other users requires at least the Member workspace role (or Admin); it is the lowest-privilege role that allows it.

  • Option B, db_owner for Warehouse1: it is a database role of the warehouse; it does not control sharing of workspace items.
  • Option C, Contributor: it can create and edit content, but cannot share items with other users.
  • Option D, Admin: it allows sharing, but grants more privileges than needed; it violates least privilege.
  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces in Microsoft Fabric

links.t: Roles in workspaces in Microsoft Fabric

q212.stem:
You have a semantic model that contains the following tables: Sales, Product and Location.

You are creating a DAX measure named Measure1 that will calculate the percentage of all the sales of a selected product. Measure1 will use the following DAX formula.

[Percentage of All Product Sales] =
DIVIDE(
    [Total Sales Amount],
    CALCULATE(
        [Total Sales Amount],
        REMOVEFILTERS ( 'Product' )
    )
)

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Statement 1: No
  • Statement 2: Yes
  • Statement 3: Yes

1 – No. DIVIDE handles division by zero and returns BLANK instead of an error.

2 – Yes. The numerator is the selected product's sales and the denominator is the sales of all products; DIVIDE returns their quotient as a decimal value (which can be formatted as a percentage).

3 – Yes. REMOVEFILTERS('Product') inside CALCULATE removes the filters on the Product table, so the denominator is evaluated with that modified filter context.

  • Official documentation: REMOVEFILTERS function (DAX), DIVIDE function (DAX)

links.t: REMOVEFILTERS function (DAX)
DIVIDE function (DAX)

q213.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace that contains a large warehouse.

You plan to create a lakehouse named Lakehouse1 for a sales dataset. Lakehouse1 will contain the following tables:

  • Sales: contains sales transactions.
  • Stores: contains a unique list of store names and locations.
  • Loyalty: contains a list of customers and their preferred stores.
  • Customers: contains a unique list of customer names and addresses.
  • Products: contains a unique list of available products and their descriptions.

You need to configure a star schema for Lakehouse1. Which table should you define as the fact table, and which type of relationship should you configure from the Sales table to the Customers table?

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Fact table: Sales
  • Relationship: Many-to-one

Why it is correct: In a star schema the fact table is the one that records measurable transactions (Sales); the others (Stores, Customers, Products) are dimensions with unique lists. The relationship from the fact table to a dimension is many-to-one: many Sales rows (several purchases) point to a single customer.

  • Fact table, Sales: the fact table records the measurable transactions: Sales; the others (Stores, Customers, Products) are dimensions.
  • Relationship, Many-to-one: from the fact table to a dimension the relationship is many-to-one: many Sales rows point to a single customer.

Incorrect options:

  • Fact table, Customers — Why it is incorrect: Customers is a dimension with one unique row per customer.
  • Fact table, Products — Why it is incorrect: Products is a dimension with one unique row per product.
  • Fact table, Stores — Why it is incorrect: Stores is a dimension with one unique row per store.
  • Relationship, One-to-one — Why it is incorrect: one-to-one is incorrect: a customer can have many sales.
  • Relationship, One-to-many — Why it is incorrect: one-to-many is the same relationship seen from the dimension (Customers → Sales), not from Sales to Customers.
  • Official documentation: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI

links.t: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI

q214.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a warehouse named Warehouse1 and a lakehouse named Lakehouse1. Warehouse1 contains a table named Table1. Lakehouse1 contains a delta table named Table2.

You need to persist data from Table1 to Table2. The solution must use a low-code interface.

What should you do?
options: Use a notebook to read the data from Table2 and insert the data into Table1.
Use a notebook to read the data from Table1 and insert the data into Table2.
Use a Dataflow Gen2 to read the data from Table1 and insert the data into Table2.
Use stored procedure to read the data from Table2 and insert the data into Table1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Use a Dataflow Gen2 to read the data from Table1 and insert the data into Table2.

Why it is correct: Dataflow Gen2 is Fabric's low-code tool (Power Query): it reads Table1 from the warehouse and loads it into Table2 in the lakehouse by using the lakehouse as the destination.

  • Option A, notebook from Table2 to Table1: it reverses the direction of the load and also requires code (PySpark/SQL), so it is not low-code.
  • Option B, notebook from Table1 to Table2: the direction is right, but a notebook requires writing code; it is not a low-code solution.
  • Option D, stored procedure from Table2 to Table1: it reverses the direction of the load and requires T-SQL, that is, code.
  • Official documentation: Dataflow Gen2 overview

links.t: Dataflow Gen2 overview

q215.stem:
You have a Microsoft Power BI semantic model that contains a table named Date. Date contains the following data.

You need to ensure that the visuals that use the Date table appear in chronological order. The solution must minimize administrative effort.

What should you do?
options: Sort the Month Number column by Column.
Sort the visuals by using the Sort ascending option on Fiscal Month.
Sort the Fiscal Month column by Column.
Sort the Date table by Column.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option C: Sort the Fiscal Month column by Column.

Why it is correct: With Sort by column you configure once, in the model, that Fiscal Month is sorted by Month Number; every visual that uses Fiscal Month then shows chronological order without individual adjustments.

  • Option A, sort Month Number by Column: the column to be sorted is Fiscal Month (by Month Number), not the other way around.
  • Option B, sort the visuals: it must be repeated in every visual and would sort Fiscal Month alphabetically, not chronologically.
  • Option D, sort the Date table by Column: tables are not sorted by column in Power BI; Sort by column applies to a single column.
  • Official documentation: Sort one column by another column in Power BI

links.t: Sort one column by another column in Power BI

q216.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a semantic model named Model1. Model1 contains a fact table named FactSales. FactSales has a relationship to a dimension table named DimDate on a column named OrderDate.

To FactSales, you add a second relationship between FactSales and DimDate based on a column named ShippedDate.

You need to filter by using ShippedDate in a new report. The solution must NOT affect the function of existing reports.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
options: Disable the ShippedDate relationship between the tables.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option D: Use a USERELATIONSHIP DAX function.
  • Option E: Disable the ShippedDate relationship between the tables.

Why it is correct: only one relationship can be active at a time between the same two tables (FactSales and DimDate), because the engine needs a single, unambiguous default path to propagate filters. Since existing reports depend on the active relationship on OrderDate and the requirement is not to affect them:

Disable the ShippedDate relationship (option E): the second relationship between FactSales[ShippedDate] and DimDate must stay inactive (dashed line in model view). That way, all existing calculations and reports keep using OrderDate unchanged.

Use USERELATIONSHIP (option D): to filter the new report's measures by ship date without changing the default relationship, define measures with CALCULATE and USERELATIONSHIP(FactSales[ShippedDate], DimDate[Date]). The function activates the inactive relationship only while that measure is evaluated.

  • Option A, enable the ShippedDate relationship: two active relationships between FactSales and DimDate cannot exist at the same time; the OrderDate one would have to be deactivated first, altering existing reports and breaking the requirement.
  • Option B, RELATEDTABLE: it returns related rows following only the active relationship in the current row context; it cannot activate or redirect the filter to an inactive relationship.
  • Option C, CROSSFILTER: it only temporarily changes the cross-filter direction of a relationship (or disables it with None); it does not replace the active relationship with another one on different columns. To use an inactive relationship, the official guidance is USERELATIONSHIP.
  • Official documentation: Active vs inactive relationship guidance, USERELATIONSHIP function (DAX), Create and manage relationships in Power BI Desktop, RELATEDTABLE function (DAX), CROSSFILTER function (DAX)

links.t: Active vs inactive relationship guidance
USERELATIONSHIP function (DAX)
Create and manage relationships in Power BI Desktop

CROSSFILTER function (DAX)

q217.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant.

You need to create a semantic model that delivers fast report rendering, minimizes query latency, and maximizes flexibility for DAX calculations.

Which storage mode should you select?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Direct Lake.

Why it is correct: Direct Lake reads Delta files in OneLake directly without copying data or translating queries to an external source: it offers performance close to Import, low latency and full DAX support.

  • Option A, Import: it copies the data into the model and needs scheduled refresh; it does not directly use the Delta files in OneLake.
  • Option C, Composite mode: it combines several modes and adds complexity; it is unnecessary when Direct Lake meets the requirement.
  • Option D, DirectQuery: it translates every query to the source, with higher latency and DAX limitations compared with Direct Lake.
  • Official documentation: Direct Lake overview

links.t: Direct Lake overview

q218.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 and a user named User1.

You need to ensure that User1 can perform the following tasks in Workspace1: create dashboards, publish semantic models, and create and publish reports. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

Which workspace role should you assign to User1?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Contributor.

Why it is correct: The Contributor role can create and edit content (reports, dashboards, semantic models) and publish it to the workspace; it is the lowest-privilege role that covers the requested tasks.

  • Option B, Member: it adds sharing and access-management permissions that are not required; more privilege than needed.
  • Option C, Viewer: it is read-only: it cannot create or publish content.
  • Option D, Admin: it grants full control of the workspace; it far exceeds least privilege.
  • Official documentation: Roles in workspaces in Microsoft Fabric

links.t: Roles in workspaces in Microsoft Fabric

q219.stem:
You are designing a Fabric semantic model named Model1 for a financial analytics workspace. Model1 includes a DAX measure named Measure1 that returns total sales.

You have a table named Currency that contains a column named Format. The Format column defines currency formatting strings for each record as follows: $#,##0.00, €#,##0.00, or ¥#,##0.00.

You have a report that uses the Currency column to identify which symbol and format string to display. In the report, Measure1 must appear with two decimal places and the appropriate currency symbol based on the selected value in the Currency column.

You create the following DAX formula: FORMAT = SELECTEDVALUE( 'Currency'[Format] )

You need to ensure that Measure1 appears correctly in visuals. The solution must minimize logic duplication.

What should you do?
options: Create a dynamic format string for Measure1 that references the FORMAT measure.
For Model1, set the data category of Measure1 to Country/Region.
For Model1, set the format type of Measure1 to Currency.
Copy the DAX expression from the Format column and paste the expression into the format string expression of Measure1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option A: Create a dynamic format string for Measure1 that references the FORMAT measure.

Why it is correct: A dynamic format string lets a DAX expression determine Measure1's format; by making it return the FORMAT measure, the symbol and decimals change with the selected currency without duplicating logic.

  • Option B, data category Country/Region: it only classifies the field (for example, for maps); it does not change the number format by currency.
  • Option C, format type Currency: it applies a fixed format that does not change with the user selection.
  • Option D, copy the DAX expression: it duplicates logic instead of referencing the FORMAT measure and stops following the selection if the source changes.
  • Official documentation: Dynamic format strings in Power BI

links.t: Dynamic format strings in Power BI

q220.stem:
You have a data warehouse that contains the tables DimCustomer, DimEmployee, DimGeography and FactInternetSales. Each table has a primary key and the following relationships: CustomerKey = FactInternetSales.CustomerKey; EmployeeKey = FactInternetSales.EmployeeKey; Geography = DimCustomer.GeographyKey.

You have a T-SQL query named Query1 that contains the following statements.

SELECT
    c.CustomerKey,
    c.FirstName,
    c.LastName,
    g.CountryRegionCode,
    g.EnglishCountryRegionName AS Country,
    e.EmployeeKey,
    e.FirstName AS SalesPersonFirstName,
    e.LastName AS SalesPersonLastName,
    f.SalesOrderNumber,
    f.OrderDate,
    f.SalesAmount
FROM FactInternetSales AS f
INNER JOIN DimCustomer AS c
    ON f.CustomerKey = c.CustomerKey
INNER JOIN DimEmployee AS e
    ON f.EmployeeKey = e.EmployeeKey
INNER JOIN DimGeography AS g
    ON c.GeographyKey = g.GeographyKey;

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Statement 1: Yes
  • Statement 2: No
  • Statement 3: No

1 – Yes. The query starts from the fact table: it returns one row per sale, so a customer with several orders appears several times.

2 – No. With INNER JOIN only rows that match in both tables are returned; if the customer's GeographyKey does not exist in DimGeography, their sales disappear from the result (a LEFT JOIN would be needed).

3 – No. Adding only a GROUP BY calculates nothing: the query has many non-aggregated columns in the SELECT and, without a function such as SUM(f.SalesAmount), it would fail.

  • Official documentation: GROUP BY (Transact-SQL), Joins

links.t: GROUP BY (Transact-SQL)
Joins

q221.stem:
You have a Fabric tenant that contains a lakehouse named LH1 and a notebook. You have a Parquet file named invoice1 that contains a column named InvoiceDateKey of the timestamp data type.

You need to create a PySpark script that will import invoice1 and create a table named fact_sale in LH1. A new column named Year must be added to fact_sale and the values in Year must use the InvoiceDateKey column.

How should you complete the script? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • First blank: withColumn
  • Second blank: col

Why it is correct: df.withColumn('Year', year(col("InvoiceDateKey"))) adds the Year column by computing the year of the timestamp; col("InvoiceDateKey") turns the column name into a Column object accepted by year(). The table is then saved in delta format partitioned by Year.

  • First blank, withColumn: df.withColumn('Year', …) adds the Year column computed from the timestamp's year.
  • Second blank, col: col("InvoiceDateKey") turns the name into a Column object, which is what year() accepts.

Incorrect options:

  • First blank, transform — Why it is incorrect: transform applies a function to a whole DataFrame; it does not add a calculated column.
  • First blank, withColumnRenamed — Why it is incorrect: withColumnRenamed only renames an existing column; it does not create Year.
  • First blank, withMetadata — Why it is incorrect: withMetadata changes a column's metadata; it does not add a new column.
  • Second blank, extract — Why it is incorrect: extract is not a PySpark function for getting the year from a column.
  • Second blank, lit — Why it is incorrect: lit creates a constant value; it does not read the InvoiceDateKey column.
  • Official documentation: How to use Microsoft Fabric notebooks

links.t: How to use Microsoft Fabric notebooks

q222.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains the following items: a warehouse named Warehouse1, a semantic model named Model1 and an interactive report named Report1.

You need to allow a user named User1 to access a single table in Warehouse1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

What should you do first?
options: Assign the Viewer role to User1 for Workspace1.
Assign object-level permissions to User1 for Warehouse1.
Assign the db_datareader role to User1 for Warehouse1.

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Share Warehouse1 with User1.

Why it is correct: To give access to a single item without adding the user to the workspace, the first step is to share Warehouse1 with User1 (this grants connect access). You then grant specific permissions on the table (for example GRANT SELECT), which meets least privilege.

  • Option A, Viewer role for Workspace1: it gives access to all items in the workspace, not only Warehouse1.
  • Option C, object-level permissions: they are not a valid first step: the user has no connection access to the warehouse yet.
  • Option D, db_datareader role: it would give read access to all tables, and the user has no access to the warehouse yet.
  • Official documentation: Share your warehouse and manage permissions

links.t: Share your warehouse and manage permissions

q223.stem:
You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that contains a semantic model and a report named Report1. Workspace1 is connected to a Git repository named Git1.

You have a deployment pipeline that contains three stages named Development, Test, and Production.

You need to publish Report1 to the Production stage.

What should you do?

answer.correct:
Correct answer:

  • Option B: Run a full deployment.

Why it is correct: in the Fabric ALM flow, when the development workspace (Workspace1) is connected to Git1 and linked to a deployment pipeline with three stages (Development, Test and Production), items are promoted to the higher stages by running the pipeline.

Dependency resolution: Workspace1 holds Report1 and the semantic model it depends on. In a deployment pipeline you cannot publish a report to a target stage if its semantic model does not already exist there.

Full promotion to production: with a full deployment (Development → Test → Production) Fabric deploys the semantic model and Report1 together, so the report reaches Production with all its dependencies intact.

  • Option A, Git commit: it saves Workspace1 changes to the linked Git1 branch, but does not publish or deploy anything to the Test or Production stages.
  • Option C, sync Workspace1 with Git1: it only keeps the development workspace aligned with its repository branch; it does not transfer items to the Test or Production workspaces.
  • Option D, backward deployment: it copies content in the opposite direction, from a later stage to an earlier empty one; the goal is to promote Report1 forward to Production.
  • Official documentation: Deploy content using deployment pipelines, Get started with deployment pipelines, Git integration process, Introduction to Git integration

links.t: Deploy content using deployment pipelines
Get started with deployment pipelines
Git integration process
Introduction to Git integration
